alarms.data_tree_path: ACU*->I/O Configuration->Noise Detector->Electrical noise detected
alarms.long_description: Electrical noise has been detected in the ECS system
alarms.cause: - One or more ECS components has intermittent and/or oscillating electric leakage to ship's ground, or\n- ECS system has been subjected to electrical noise from an external source
alarms.effect:
No immediate effect
The fault can generate other consequential alarms in the ECS system, e.g. 
- Exh. Valve Closed Position Changed
- Exh. Valve closing/opening too fast/slow (4 alarms)
- Illegal ELFI/FIVA Position
- ELFI/FIVA Feedback Signal Failure

NOTE: 
Never ignore this alarm. Safety critical issues may arise.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Noise pulse counter by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation
- Cabling, sensors, actuators, Controllers for loose connections or intermittent and/or oscillating electric leakages/short circuits to ground.

To locate an intermittent and/or oscillating electric leakage to ship's ground:
1.Stop engine or reduce rpm to slow down level
If the ACU1 Controller is equipped with IRM Module go to step 7
2. On one controller: Disconnect power supply Connector J1
3. Observe if increase in noise pulse counter has stopped
4. If the increase has stopped, the Controller with intermittent and/or oscillating electric leakage to ship's
ground has been found  skip step 5 and continue to step 6
5. Reconnect the power supply Connector J1 in order for the controller to resume normal function and go back to
step 2, choosing the next controller
6. Reconnect the power supply Connector J1  the controller will resume normal function.
7. Set the ACU1 Controller in TEST MODE by pressing MPC mode button on MOP Maintenance -> System view
I/O. This will stop the controllers normal function.
8. Disconnect connections one at a time (from J2 to J85, - NOT J1), and after each disconnection observe if
increase in noise pulse counter has stopped
9. If increase has stopped, the cable, sensor or actuator with loose connections or intermittent and/or
oscillating electric leakages/short circuits to ground, has been located
10.Revert to basic electrical trouble shooting to repair
11.Set the ACU1 Controller in NORNAL MODE by pressing MPC mode button on MOP Maintenance -> System view I/O

NOTE: 
If a CCU is disconnected or stopped for more than 20 minutes, establishing of emergency lubrication to the affected cylinder is recommended, by fitting of backup lubrication cables from ECU.

alarms.cause: One or more ECS components have increased electric leakage to ship's ground.
alarms.effect: No immediate effect. The alarm can be an indication of beginning deterioration of system components.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Insulation  level by observing the display on the insulation monitor, or
-Insulation level by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation
- Insulation  level trend in CoCoS-EDS if applicable 
- Individual insulation of ECS components (sensors, controllers, actuators, cabling) to determine the cause of leakage
- Refer to ECS trouble shooting guide "test for earth failure in ECS system" for further trouble shooting advise

alarms.long_description: The alarm indicates that the signal from the sensor connected to the specified channel is outside the legal range. The sensor should give a signal between 4 mA to 20 mA.
alarms.cause: Most probably a failure in the cabling to the sensor, or\nfailure of the sensor, or missing sensor power supply, or\nfailure of the input of the ACU1 Controller.
alarms.effect:
Reduced system performance.
Reduced supervision.

NOTE 
Never ignore this alarm. Safety critical issues may arise.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check the cabling to the sensor, according to the installation drawings.
Check that the sensor has sufficient power supply (if it is a 2-wire sensor, the supply is integrated in the signal). 
Check the current into terminal "C" of the channel. It must be within 4 mA and 20 mA. 
If the current is above or below the range, the current out of the sensor must be checked.
If the current into the ACU1 Controller is within the range, while the alarm is present, the ACU1 Controller may be damaged and must be replaced.

alarms.long_description: Electric motor cannot be controlled by the engine control system
alarms.cause:
- Electric motor switchboard is off or manually set to 'Local', or
- Electric motor switch board failure, or
- Switchboard feedback failure, or
- Cabling failure
alarms.effect: If the failure is in the feedback part only: No effect\nElse: No ECS control of electric motor
alarms.suggested_action:
1. Check that the operation control switch at the switchboard is set to ''Remote'
2. Check switchboard, main breaker and overcurrent protection relay
3. Check cabling

If all is OK: Set switch to 'Off' and wait a few seconds. 
Reset switch to ''Remote'

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU*->Advanced Liner Wall Monitoring->CCU1-Unstable Liner Wall Temp
alarms.long_description: LWM - Unstable liner surface temperatures
alarms.cause: - Possible scuffing indication.
alarms.effect: - Extensive Cylinder Liner Wear.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Increase cylinder oil feed-rate.
- Decrease Pmax for the unit in question.
- Reduce chief index limit on specific cylinder in relation to actual engine load.
- Perform drain oil analysis, all units.
- Perform piston ring inspection at first opportunity.

alarms.long_description: LWM - Unstable liner surface temperatures- TT 8820
alarms.cause: - Possible scuffing indication.
alarms.effect: - Extensive Cylinder Liner Wear.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Increase cylinder oil feed-rate.
- Decrease Pmax for the unit in question.
- Reduce chief index limit on specific cylinder in relation to actual engine load.
- Perform drain oil analysis, all units.
- Perform piston ring inspection at first opportunity.

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU*->TC Cut Out->Supervision->Closing TCV Time Out
alarms.long_description: Turbocharger cut out operation has timed out when trying to close the Turbine Cut Out Valve.
alarms.cause: - Failure on air supply to valves.\n- Valve failure.\n- Signal or cabling failure on the valve feedback or setpoint.
alarms.effect: Turbocharger cut out cancelled by ECS. ECS will now open the Turbine Cut Out Valve. Compressor Cut Out Valve and EGR Blower Bypass Valve will remain open.
alarms.suggested_action: Investigate Turbine Cut Out Valve.

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU*->TC Cut Out->Supervision->Opening TCV Time Out
alarms.long_description: Turbocharger cut in operation has timed out when trying to open the Turbine Cut Out Valve.
alarms.cause: - Failure on air supply to valves.\n- Valve failure.\n- Signal or cabling failure on the valve feedback or setpoint.
alarms.effect: Turbocharger cut in cancelled by ECS. ECS will now close the Turbine Cut Out Valve and then close the Compressor Cut Out Valve and EGR Blower Bypass Valve.
alarms.suggested_action: Investigate Turbine Cut Out Valve.

alarms.synopsis: Closing CCV and BBV Time Out
alarms.data_tree_path: ACU*->TC Cut Out->Supervision->Closing CCV and BBV Time Out
alarms.long_description: Turbocharger cut out operation has timed out when trying to close the Compressor Cut Out Valve and EGR Blower Bypass Valve.
alarms.cause: - Failure on air supply to valves.\n- Valve failure.\n- Signal or cabling failure on the valve feedback or setpoint.
alarms.effect: Turbocharger cut out cancelled by ECS. ECS will now open the Compressor Cut Out Valve and EGR Blower Bypass Valve and then open the Turbine Cut Out Valve.
alarms.suggested_action: Investigate Compressor Cut Out Valve and EGR Blower Bypass Valve.

alarms.synopsis: Opening CCV and BBV Time Out
alarms.data_tree_path: ACU*->TC Cut Out->Supervision->Opening CCV and BBV Time Out
alarms.long_description: Turbocharger cut in operation has timed out when trying to open the Compressor Cut Out Valve and EGR Blower Bypass Valve.
alarms.cause: - Failure on air supply to valves.\n- Valve failure.\n- Signal or cabling failure on the valve feedback or setpoint.
alarms.effect: Turbocharger cut in cancelled by ECS. ECS will now close the Compressor Cut Out Valve and EGR Blower Bypass Valve. Turbine Cut Out Valve will remain closed.
alarms.suggested_action: Investigate Compressor Cut Out Valve and EGR Blower Bypass Valve.

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU*->TC Cut Out->Supervision->TC Cut Out/In Operation Failed
alarms.long_description: Turbocharger cut out/in operation has failed to reach a state of either all TCCO valves open or all TCCO valves closed.
alarms.cause: - Failure on air supply to valves.\n- Valve failure.\n- Signal or cabling failure on the valve feedback or setpoint.
alarms.effect: - Compressor is cut in while Turbine is cut out. Turbocharger will run in reverse and might get damaged.\n- ECS changes to Turbocharger Cut Out state and sets all TCCO valve setpoints to close.
alarms.suggested_action: - Keep engine load low to protect turbocharger.\n- Investigate Turbine Cut Out Valve, Compressor Cut Out Valve and EGR Blower Bypass Valve.

alarms.effect: TC Cut Out not valid. Risk of TC damage.
alarms.suggested_action: - Slow down engine.\n- Investigate Turbine Cut Out Valve.

alarms.effect: - Turbine is cut in while compressor might be cut out. Risk of turbine overspeed!\n- Cancellable slowdown activated.
alarms.suggested_action: - Slow down engine.\n- Investigate Turbine Cut Out Valve.

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU*->TC Cut Out->Supervision->TCCO Valve Position Invalid
alarms.long_description: The combined position of Turbocharger Cut Out valves is invalid.
alarms.cause:
- Valve is manually being operated.
- Failure on air supply to valves.
- Valve failure.
- Signal or cabling failure on the valve feedback.
alarms.effect: Risk of turbocharger running in reverse or overspeeding.
alarms.suggested_action: - Finish manual valve operation.\n- Slow down engine.\n- Investigate Turbocharger Cut Out valves.

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU*->CR Supply Control->Pressure Controller->CR Index Control Failure
alarms.long_description: CR Pressure Ch 33 out of range\n or CR Pressure Setpoint from ECU not valid
alarms.cause: CR Pressure sensor failure or\n -Network failure
alarms.effect: - CR pump index is forced to 100%\n - Combivalve may be activated
alarms.suggested_action: Check:\n -CR pressure sensor cabling\n -Network connection ECU ->ACU

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU*->CR Supply Control->Pressure Controller->CR Index High
alarms.long_description: CR Pump index is at near 100%
alarms.cause: - Leakage in Rail or Pipes\n - Failing pump
alarms.effect: -If pump capacity is insufficient, it can cause the fuel pressure to drop.\n -This can ultimately cause a reduction of the load or a shutdown
alarms.suggested_action: - Check of pipes and drains\n - Check CR pump\n - Check CR pump drive (VLT)

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU*->CR Supply Control->Pump Motor Control->CR Pump Motor Ctrl Failed
alarms.long_description: Electric motor cannot be controlled by the engine control system
alarms.cause:
- Electric motor switchboard is off or manually set to 'Local', or
- Electric motor switch board failure, or
- Switchboard feedback failure, or
- Cabling failure
alarms.effect: If the failure is in the feedback part only: No effect\nElse: No ECS control of electric motor
alarms.suggested_action:
1. Check that the operation control switch at the switchboard is set to 'Remote'
 2. Check switchboard, main breaker and overcurrent protection relay
 3. Check cabling
 If all is OK: Set switch to 'Off' and wait a few seconds.
 Reset switch to 'Remote'
 NOTE:
 If a pump is actually running, but ECS running signal is both missing, engine start will be blocked (start blocked).

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU*->CR Supply Control->Leakage Supervision->CR Pipe Leakage Detected
alarms.long_description: CR Fuel leakage from inner to outer pipe
alarms.cause: CR Fuel oil detected in outer pipe. i.e. the inner pipe leaks
alarms.effect: - Fuel Oil leak may affect the Pressure and the available engine load.\n- Reduced Pressure can lead to shutdown
alarms.suggested_action: Find and repair the leak

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU*->CR Supply Control->Leakage Supervision->CR Pump Leakage Detected
alarms.long_description: CR Fuel leakage in drain from Rail or CR Pump
alarms.cause: CR Fuel leakage from the CR Rail or the CR Pump
alarms.effect: Continuous operation may result in larger leakage.
alarms.suggested_action: Find and repair the leak

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU*->Lube BN Control->Lube BN Valve (NC)->Lube BN Valve Failure
alarms.long_description: Valve position deviates from commanded position
alarms.cause:
- Valve failure, or
- Feedback failure, or
- Valve actuator air supply failure, or
- Cabling failure
alarms.effect: The engine lube oil does not have the desired BN value.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Valve
- Valve feedback
- Actuator air supply
- Valve cabling

Further troubleshooting after end of dual fuel operation:
1. Operate valve by changing ACU1 Controller mode to test.
2. Observe feedback during valve operation

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU*->I/O Configuration->Ch32,1204-2,Lube Oil Pressure (bar)->Suprv. Ch32,1204-2,Lube Oil Pressur
alarms.long_description: The alarm indicates that the signal from the sensor connected to the specified channel is outside the legal range. The sensor should give a signal between 4 mA to 20 mA.
alarms.cause: Most probably a failure in the cabling to the sensor, or\nfailure of the sensor, or missing sensor power supply, or\nfailure of the input of the ACU2 Controller.
alarms.effect: Reduced supervision quality, 1 sensor out of 3 is unavailable.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check the cabling to the sensor, according to the installation drawings.
Check that the sensor has sufficient power supply (if it is a 2-wire sensor, the supply is integrated in the signal). 
Check the current into terminal "C" of the channel. It must be within 4 mA and 20 mA. 
If the current is above or below the range, the current out of the sensor must be checked.
If the current into the ACU2 Controller is within the range, while the alarm is present, the ACU2 Controller may be damaged and must be replaced.

alarms.data_tree_path: ACU->I/O Configuration->Ch30,1238-3,Prop. Valve Feedback->Suprv. Ch30,1238-3,Prop. Valve Feed
alarms.long_description: The alarm indicates that the signal from the sensor connected to the specified channel is outside the legal range. The sensor should give a signal between 4 mA to 20 mA.
alarms.cause: Most probably a failure in the cabling to the sensor, or\nfailure of the sensor, or missing sensor power supply, or\nfailure of the input of the ACU3 Controller.
alarms.effect: This will lead to pump ctrl. fault. If the pump only suffers from electrical faults, then the pump will deliver full flow in the engine rotation direction.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check the cabling to the sensor, according to the installation drawings.
Check that the sensor has sufficient power supply (if it is a 2-wire sensor, the supply is integrated in the signal). 
Check the current into terminal "C" of the channel. It must be within 4 mA and 20 mA. 
If the current is above or below the range, the current out of the sensor must be checked.
If the current into the ACU3 Controller is within the range, while the alarm is present, the ACU3 Controller may be damaged and must be replaced.

alarms.long_description: ECUA Controller is not in normal operating mode\n\nThis group alarm is raised because both EICU A and EICU B report, that the ECUA Controller is not running in normal mode (App. not running on .. ). Other alarms in the group are raised as a consequence of this condition. To view all alarms in this group: Press +/- at the bottom of the MOP screen.
alarms.cause: - ECUA Controller is restarting after power off/on.\n- ECUA Controller in test or configuration mode.\n- ECUA Controller failure.
alarms.effect: ECUA Controller not ready.\nRedundancy reduced.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check ECUA Controller mode status.

If in test or configuration mode: Restart in normal mode.

If no mode is visible: Wait for ECUA Controller to finish restart.

If the problem persists: Replace ECUA Controller.

alarms.long_description: Shutdown has been ordered.\n\nThis is a group alarm caused by a shutdown order from the safety system. Other alarms in the group are raised as a consequence of this condition. To view all alarms in this group: Press +/- at the bottom of the MOP screen.

alarms.data_tree_path: Shutdown alarm missing
alarms.long_description: Shutdown has been ordered. One or more controllers have not yet confirmed shutdown.\n\nThis is an alarm caused by a shutdown order from the safety system and one or more controllers do not report shutdown.
alarms.cause: - Shutdown feedback signal from affected controller delayed or missing, or\n- No shutdown signal from safety system
alarms.effect: One or more controllers may try to keep engine running because it may not have received the shut down signal from the safety system.
alarms.suggested_action: Check:\n- Controllers, that have not confirmed the shutdown. Power off, if necessary.\n- Cabling and signal from safety system to J32 for CCUs and J34 for ECUs.

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Tacho set A failure
alarms.long_description: Abnormal tacho set A signals on multiple CCUs/ECUs .\n\nThis group alarm is caused by multiple 'Tacho set A failure' alarms. Other alarms in the group are raised as a consequence of this condition. To view the alarms in the group: Press +/- at the bottom of the MOP screen.
alarms.cause:
- Cabling failure (loose connection etc.), or
- Turning wheel sensor failure, or
- Encoder failure, or
- Tacho amplifier A failure, or
- Sensor support console failure, or
- Power failure (ECUA powers tacho set A)

If trigger ring is fitted, this alarm may be caused by:
- Trigger/marker ring is damaged, or
- Trigger/marker sensor failure
alarms.effect: The CCUs/ECUs has switched to tacho set B. \nRedundancy reduced.
alarms.suggested_action:
If only one ECU or CCU reports failure: Check Connector J40-J43 on failing unit.
If OK: Replace ECU or CCU

If all CCUs and ECUs report tacho A failure, check tacho signals on maintenance screen and power to tacho amplifier TCA-A: 
   1. Check power on the tacho amplifier TSA-A connector J5 pin (J,A) J=24V A=0V.
   2. Turn the engine minimum one revolution (by turning gear) 
   3. On failing ECU or CCU maintenance screen: Check that channel 40-43 toggle correctly between true and false    
       Channel 40 + 41: twice per revolution 
       Channel 42 + 43: multiple times per revolution (360) 

Perform tacho test on MOP:
Go to Maintenance  -> Function Test -> Tacho 
Follow tacho test instructions

Trace the error by following the signal from :
     Encoder and/or turning wheel marker sensor
        ->Amplifier (TSA-A)
        ->ECU A (supplying power to TSA-A from connector J40 pin (D,A) D=24V A=0V)

If trigger ring is fitted, check:
      a. Trigger/marker ring
      b. Trigger/marker sensor

alarms.suggested_action:
If only one ECU or CCU reports failure: Check Connector J44-J47 on failing unit.
If OK: Replace ECU or CCU

If all CCUs and ECUs report tacho B failure, check tacho signals on maintenance screen and power to tacho amplifier TCA-B:
   1. Check power on the tacho amplifier TSA-B connector J5 pin (J,A) J=24V A=0V.
   2. Turn the engine minimum one revolution (by turning gear)
   3. On failing ECU or CCU maintenance screen: Check that channel 44-47 toggle correctly between true and false
       Channel 44 + 45: twice per revolution
       Channel 46 + 47: multiple times per revolution (360)

Perform tacho test on MOP:
Go to Maintenance  -> Function Test -> Tacho 
Follow tacho test instructions

Trace the error by following the signal from :
     Encoder and/or turning wheel marker sensor
        ->Amplifier (TSA-B)
        ->ECU B (supplying power to TSA-B from connector J40 pin (D,A) D=24V A=0V)

alarms.synopsis: GROUP: Delta Tacho B too big
alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Delta Tacho B too big
alarms.long_description: Abnormal angle difference between tacho system A and B\n\nThis group alarm is caused by 'Delta Tacho B too big'. To view all alarms in the group: Press +/- at the bottom of the MOP screen.
alarms.cause: The angle between tacho set A and B marker signal exceeds the limit.
alarms.effect: If the system switches from tacho set A to B, maximum pressure deviation may occur.
alarms.suggested_action:
If the alarm 'Tacho set A failure' or 'Tacho set B failure' is active: Ignore this alarm. 

If this alarm is the only tacho alarm:
- Check and adjust Pmax. 
- At first opportunity: 
     1. Inspect the mechanical condition of the encoders. 
     2. Readjust the encoders
     3. Perform tacho test on MOP:
         Go to 'Maintenance ' -> 'Function Test' -> 'Tacho' 
         Follow tacho test instructions

NOTE
If encoder A is readjusted or replaced: Perform PMI measurement, and restore tacho offset settings according to 0-diagram

Reactivate fuel injection, go to 'Engine' -> 'Status' -> 'Cylinder Value Status' -> 'HCU Status and Reset' to reset failing unit. 
Do not reactivate fuel injection until the cylinder unit is considered to be OK.
Reactivation only possibly for speed below 'HCU ReEnable Max Speed'

If the problem persists replace or exchange, one part at a time: 
- ELFI / FIVA valve
- CCU

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Illegal ELFI/FIVA set point (CCU12) [SLD]
alarms.long_description:
Illegal internal ELFI/FIVA set point.
Risk of untimed fuel injection.

This group alarm is caused by 'Illegal ELFI/FIVA set point'.  
Other alarms in the group are raised as a consequence of this condition. To view all alarms in the group: Press +/- at the bottom of the MOP screen.
alarms.cause: Internal CCU failure
alarms.effect:
No fuel injection due to risk of untimed fuel injection.

For FIVA installations:
- No exhaust valve operation 
- Slowdown is requested
alarms.suggested_action: If the alarm is activated during normal engine operation: Replace CCU

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: FIVA Amplifier Current Supervision (CCU1) [SLD]
alarms.long_description: Amplifier current deviates from the current ordered by the CCU
alarms.cause:
- Accumulator pressure too low, or 
- De-aerating orifice in exhaust valve top blocked, or  
- Non-return valves for exhaust valve actuator oil inlet damaged, or
- No air supply or leaking exhaust valve air spring, or
- Exhaust valve position sensor failure, or
- ELVA/FIVA valve failure
- Amplifier failure, or
- CCU failure
alarms.effect: Fuel injection stopped on affected cylinder \nSlow-down is requested.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Exhaust valve position sensor
- Accumulator pressure
- De-aerating orifice in exhaust valve top
- Non-return valves for exhaust valve actuator oil inlet
- Air spring supply pressure and perform drop-down test of exhaust valve spindle.
- ELFI / FIVA valve
- Amplifier 
- CCU

To run amplifier function test :
1. Stop the engine at first opportunity
2. Go to 'Maintenance' -> 'Function test' -> 'HCU'
3. Perform amplifier test

Further troubleshooting: 
1. Stop the engine at first opportunity. 
2. Go to 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'HCU'
3. Activate 'Fuel Plunger' and 'Exhaust Valve' to test failing unit

alarms.synopsis: GROUP: FIVA Amplifier Thermal Protection Active (CCU1) [SLD]
alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: FIVA Amplifier Thermal Protection Active (CCU1) [SLD]
alarms.long_description: Amplifier has shut down due to too high FIVA current consumption\n\nThis group alarm is raised because Amplifier has reached the current limit. Other alarms in the group are raised as a consequence of this condition. To view all alarms in this group: Press +/- at the bottom of the MOP screen.
alarms.cause:
- FIVA failure, or 
- Cabling failure, or 
- Amplifier failure, or
- CCU fuse (F9) for amplifier is blown
alarms.effect: No fuel injection. \nNo exhaust valve operation. \nSlowdown is requested
alarms.suggested_action:
1. Check FIVA cabling
2. Stop the engine at first opportunity 
3. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'HCU' 
4. Test failing unit's injection and exhaust valve operation 
5. Compare signals from failing unit to signals from a well functioning unit
6. Reduce 'Chief Index limit [%]' first and then Re-enable HCU:
   
   'Chief Limiters' -> 'Chief Index limit [%]' below 40 %.
   'Status' -> 'Cylinder Value Status' -> 'HCU Status and reset' Reset 'Fault' button.
   Set again 'Chief Index limit [%]' to the same value as before. 

If the problem persists replace or exchange, one part at a time: 
- FIVA valve
- FIVA amplifier 
- FIVA cabling
- CCU

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Hydraulic pressure sensor ACU1 deviates
alarms.long_description: Hydraulic oil pressure sensor (1201-x) on this ACU deviates from the hydraulic oil pressure sensors on the two other ACUs.
alarms.cause:
a. Hydraulic pump failure, or
b. Sensor failure, or
c. ECU Controller failure, or 
d. Cable failure
alarms.effect:
If a:
Engine performance may be reduced due to reduced hydraulic capacity.

If b, c, and d:
No effect on engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:

a. Hydraulic pump
b. Cabling
c. ECU Controller
d. Sensor

If a, hydraulic pump failure:
1. Reduce engine load until stable engine performance is achieved
2. Check other alarms
3. Check pump and pump drive shaft

If b, c, or d:
Repair or replace failing part

alarms.synopsis: GROUP: Large deviation from model curve
alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Large deviation from model curve
alarms.long_description: Swash plate follow pump set points deviate too much from the model curve
alarms.cause:
- Hydraulic leak, or 
- Swash plate pump failure (hydraulic failure, broken pump shaft etc.), or
- Proportional valve failure, or
- ECU Controller failure, or
- Proportional valve amplifier failure (if fitted)

NOTE
This alarm may occur during wind milling. In this case, this alarm can be ignored.
alarms.effect: Engine performance and HPS pressure may be reduced.\nEngine will shut down, if the HPS pressure drops below shutdown level.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Hydraulic system for leaks 
- Swash plate pumps for mechanical failures
- Proportional valves

Perform HPS function test on MOP: 'Maintenance' -> 'Function Test'

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Changing pressure controling pump
alarms.long_description: Pressure controlling pump automatically switched
alarms.cause:
- No position feedback signal from proportional valve, or 
- No swash plate position feedback signal, or 
- Proportional valve amplifier failure, or 
- Mechanical pump failure
alarms.effect:
ECS will attempt to deliver full flow:
 - Full flow ahead, if engine runs ahead
 - Full flow astern, if engine runs astern

If two or more pumps fail:
Engine may not be able to run astern.

In case of mechanical pump failure: ECS may deliver low or no flow to the HPS.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check cabling to and from: 
- Proportional valve
- Proportional valve amplifier
- LVDT amplifier 
- ECU Controller 
     
Check pump and proportional valve

Go to 'Auxiliaries' -> 'Hydraulic System' -> 'Failed pump' to reset failure state.

Further troubleshooting:
1. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'HPS'
2. Test failing pump swashplate operation.
3. Compare signals from failing pump to signals from a well functioning pump.

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Torque limiter cancelled
alarms.long_description:
Swash plate pump torque limit is cancelled.

NOTE
NEVER cancel pump torque limiter, unless one or more swash plate pumps do not deliver sufficient flow.
alarms.cause: Pump torque restriction has been cancelled manually (Chief-level access required).
alarms.effect: No pump torque restrictions
alarms.suggested_action: Enable the torque limiter as soon as the problem is  solved.

alarms.suggested_action: Switch back to automatic control as soon as manual operation is completed

- Local pressure gauge on start-up pumps
- For hydraulic leakages

alarms.synopsis: GROUP: Hydraulic pressure deviates from setpoint
alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Hydraulic pressure deviates from setpoint
alarms.long_description: The hydraulic pressure deviates from the hydraulic pressure set point calculated by the engine control system
alarms.cause: - Hydraulic system leakage, or\n- Engine driven pump failure, or\n- Engine driven pump calibration failure
alarms.effect: If the hydraulic pressure is lower than the ECS computed setpoint and it continues to decrease, the hydraulic pumps cannot deliver enough oil to maintain the pressure. If the pressure drops below 145 - 150 bar, the ECS is likely to carry out a shutdown. If the pressure is too high, it could lead to increased injection pressure.
alarms.suggested_action:
Reduce engine load until stable engine performance is achieved.

Check:
- Hydraulic system for leaks
- Engine driven pump

If the problem persists: Recalibrate engine driven pump on MOP

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Pump inlet pressure low
alarms.long_description: Lubrication oil inlet  pressure is low.
alarms.cause: - Sensor failure, or\n- Lubrication oil supply pump(s) not running, or \n- Inlet valve closed
alarms.effect:
No effect.

NOTE
If system oil pressure drops below shutdown level: 
Engine control system will request shutdown.
alarms.suggested_action: Check:\n- Inlet pressure sensors \n- Lubrication oil supply system(pumps, valves, etc)

alarms.synopsis: GROUP: Pump inlet pressure shutdown level
alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Pump inlet pressure shutdown level
alarms.long_description: Lubrication oil inlet  pressure is below shutdown level.
alarms.cause: - Failing pressure sensors, or\n- Lubrication oil supply pump(s) not running, or \n- Inlet valve closed
alarms.effect: Engine control system has requested a non-cancellable shutdown to protect the HPS pumps.
alarms.suggested_action: Check:\n- Inlet pressure sensors \n- Lubrication oil supply system(pumps, valves, etc)

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: No pump inlet sensors
alarms.long_description: No pump inlet sensors available
alarms.cause: Sensors out of signal range or cabling is malfunctioning
alarms.effect: Engine will shut down
alarms.suggested_action: Inspect sensors and their cabling according to electrical wiring diagram

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Hydraulic pressure shutdown level
alarms.long_description: Hydraulic oil pressure below shutdown level
alarms.cause: - Failing hydraulic oil supply, or\n- Leakage in hydraulic oil distribution system, or\n- Failing hydraulic oil pressure sensors
alarms.effect: Engine will shut down.\nIt will not be possible to start engine with too low hydraulic oil supply pressure.
alarms.suggested_action: Check:\n- Hydraulic oil supply system.\n- Hydraulic oil pressure sensors.

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Low Hydraulic Pressure
alarms.long_description: Maximum allowed fuel index is reduced due to insufficient hydraulic pressure
alarms.cause: - Pump failure, or \n- Hydraulic leakage, or\n- Bypass valve failure
alarms.effect: - Engine load may be reduced.\n- Unstable speed and fuel index. \n- Too low pressure will cause shutdown.
alarms.suggested_action:
To avoid unstable engine performance: Reduce engine load

Check for: 
- Hydraulic pump related alarms 
- Hydraulic leakages 
- Failing bypass valves

alarms.synopsis: GROUP: StartUP pump cmd state deviation
alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: StartUP pump cmd state deviation
alarms.long_description: ECU A and ECU B are generating differing output values
alarms.cause:
Deviation between redundant input signals:
- to ECU A and ECU B 
OR 
- to ACU 1, 2 and 3 
OR
- from RCS
alarms.effect: Redundancy reduced
alarms.suggested_action:
Restart the engine to reset the alarm

If the problem persists, check:
- ECU cabling 
- ACU cabling
- RCS signals

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Running Failed
alarms.long_description: The engine has stopped
alarms.cause: - Sudden torque increase at low engine speed, or\n- Fuel starvation, or\n- Engine speed too low
alarms.effect: Engine does not run.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check: 
- Fuel oil supply system
- Fuel related alarms, if any

If all OK: Restart the engine

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Starting Failed
alarms.long_description: 3 repeated starting attempts failed
alarms.cause: - Starting air system failure, or\n- Torque too high, or \n- No fuel injection
alarms.effect: Engine did not start.\nAutomatic starting sequence has finished.\nManual restart is required.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Starting air system
- Fuel oil supply system

Restart the engine

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Turning Failed
alarms.long_description: Engine slow turning attempt failed\nEngine was not turned sufficiently
alarms.cause: - Starting air system failure, or\n- ECUB is controlling
alarms.effect: Engine may not be able to start.\nSlow-turning valve is not wired to ECUB and Engine start that require slow-turning will fail.
alarms.suggested_action:
1. Check ECUA is controlling
2. Check slow turning valve
3. Turn engine by turning gear to a different position
4. Retry manual slow turn before new engine start

If the problem persists, check:
- Start air pressure
- Starting air pilot valves
- Starting valves

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Manual blower operation demanded
alarms.long_description: Operation set to 'Manual' on MOP

alarms.suggested_action: Switch back to automatic control as soon as manual operation is completed

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Insufficient blowers
alarms.long_description: Insufficient auxiliary blower capacity\n\nThis group alarm is raised because both ECU A and ECU B report, that 'Insufficient blowers capacity' has occurred. To view all alarms in this group: Press +/- at the bottom of the MOP screen.
alarms.cause: Less than half of the installed blowers are running.
alarms.effect:
Engine cannot be started from bridge control station.

NOTE
If 'Start' is initiated from ECR or LOP, engine will attempt to start even if no blowers are running.
alarms.suggested_action: 1. Check that the operation control switch at the switchboard is set to 'Remote'\n2. Check switchboard, main breaker and overcurrent protection relay\n3. Check cabling

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: DF Operation Cut Out
alarms.long_description: Dual fuel operation is cut out on cylinder
alarms.cause: Dual fuel operation cut out is activated on MOP
alarms.effect:
- Engine unable to run dual fuel optimized mode

During dual fuel operation:
- FO/SF Index Calibration in Limit alarms disabled
- Exhaust gas temperature deviation expected

WARNING!! Cylinder lubrication amount is not compensated for higher sulfur content of fuel oil on cut out cylinder.
alarms.suggested_action:
To re-enable dual fuel operation on cylinder,
go to 'Chief Limiters' -> 'Cyl. Cut Out'

RECOMMENDATION
For prolonged operation with dual fuel operation cut out activated, increase lubrication amount on cut out cylinder:
Go to: 'Auxiliaries' -> 'Cylinder Lubrication' and increase 'Feed Rate Adjust Factor'

alarms.synopsis: GROUP: Hydraulic HP Pump Failed on ACU1
alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Hydraulic HP Pump Failed on ACU1
alarms.long_description: Hydraulic high pressure pump does not work correctly
alarms.cause: - Hydraulic pump failure, or\n- EICU Controller not running in normal mode, or \n- Network failure
alarms.effect:
Swash plate moves to fail safe position (maximum flow in ahead direction) 

Running ahead: 
No effect on engine performance.
Hydraulic pressure may increase. 

Running astern: 
Reversing the engine may not be possible due to insufficient hydraulic pressure.
alarms.suggested_action: Check:\n- Other alarms to locate the root cause for the pump alarms\n- That the EICU Controller is in normal running mode

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: No Ctrl Station Selected
alarms.long_description: Inconsistent control station selection.\nNone or multiple control stations requested.
alarms.cause: - RCS and/or  RCS connection failure, or\n- Cabling failure
alarms.effect: - Engine control station is retained at current location.\n- Change of control station is only possible with "forced take".
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- RCS and connection to ECS
- Cabling

If problem persists:
- Restart EICU

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: ECR Control Station Forced
alarms.long_description: Engine control forced to ECR control station.
alarms.cause: ECR 'forced take' activated.
alarms.effect: Engine manoeuvre place is switched to ECR control station.\nOnly LOP 'forced take' can override this command.
alarms.suggested_action: No action

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Bridge Control Station Forced
alarms.long_description: Engine control forced to Bridge control station.
alarms.cause: Bridge 'forced take' activated.
alarms.effect: Engine manoeuvre place is switched to Bridge control station.
alarms.suggested_action: No action

alarms.synopsis: GROUP: Handle Stop and Stop Switch Deviation
alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Handle Stop and Stop Switch Deviation
alarms.long_description: The ECS (Engine Control System) has detected that the Handle Stop position and Stop Switch Position does not match the expected at the current selected control station.\n\nThis group alarm is raised because both EICU A and EICU B report, that the "Handle Stop position and Stop Switch Position" does not match. To view all alarms in this group: Press +/- at the bottom of the MOP screen.
alarms.cause:
- Stop switch or signal failure, or
- Analog handle or signal failure, or
- Analog handle stop is ON and Stop Switch is OFF, or
- Analog handle stop is OFF and Stop Switch is ON

Note: Analog handle Stop is ON  when handle speed set is zero RPM!
alarms.effect: Engine start can not be performed from current control station.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Analog handle signal and stop switch signal at current control station
- Stop switch
- Analog handle signal and calibration

To start engine: Change control station and activate engine start.

alarms.synopsis: GROUP: Too many HP Pump Failures
alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Too many HP Pump Failures
alarms.long_description: Two or more high pressure pumps are failing
alarms.cause:
More than one high pressure pump cannot be controlled.

NOTE
If more than 3 pumps are installed, pump 4 and 5 are controlled by the ECUs
alarms.effect: - High pressure pumps move to fail safe position (maximum flow in ahead direction)\n- Reversing the engine may not be possible due to insufficient hydraulic pressure
alarms.suggested_action:
Check other alarms to locate the root cause for the pump alarms

NOTE
NEVER ignore this alarm. Safe critical issues may arise!

alarms.cause: Actual engine speed deviate from speed set.
alarms.effect: No effect
alarms.suggested_action: Adjust speed set to move actual engine speed outside barred range.

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Shop Test Mode Active
alarms.long_description: Shop Test Mode is active
alarms.cause: Shop Test Mode can be toggled on/off from the ECT application. When it is toggled on this alarm is active.
alarms.effect:
The following changes are in effect to allow necessary shop test trials to be carried out:
1: Max Engine Speed has been increased from 105% to 110% MCR
2: Overspeed protection limit change from 106% and 108% MCR to 110% MCR
3: P-scav and Torque limiters have been cancelled
4: Chief index limiter has been raised from 110% to 120%
5: The load program has been disabled
6: Chief Max Speed parameter has been disabled

Changes 1 and 3 are only in effect when ECR is the active control station.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- EICU cabling

Reselect Shop Test Mode or Not Shop Test Mode on the ECT screen

If the problem persists:
- Restart either EICU A or EICU B when convenient

alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Cyl 1. No Cylinder lubrication
alarms.long_description: No cylinder lubrication\n\nThis group alarm is caused by 'No cylinder lubrication', reported by both EICU A and EICU B. To view all alarms in the group: Press +/- at the bottom of the MOP screen.
alarms.cause: CCU 1 is not connected to the Network
alarms.effect: - No lubrication oil is injected\n- Slowdown is requested
alarms.suggested_action:
Check CCU1 Controller mode status
If in test or configuration mode: Restart in normal mode
If no mode is visible: Wait for CCU1 Controller to finish restart
If the problem persists: Replace CCU1 Controller

alarms.long_description: Compression pressure is too low for SF injection.
alarms.cause:
- Leaking exhaust valve, or 
- Piston ring blow-by, or
- Air spring failure, or 
- Exhaust valve actuator failure, or 
- Exhaust valve damper failure, or  
- ELFI / FIVA valve failure, or
- Pcomp/Pscav offset, or
- Cylinder pressure sensor failure
alarms.effect: - Dual fuel shutdown\n- Engine operation on fuel oil
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Cylinder pressure. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'Cyl. Events'
- Alarms on MOP
- Exhaust valve closing. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'HCU Events'
- Air spring
- Exhaust valve actuator
- Exhaust valve oil cylinder
- ELFI / FIVA valve
- Pcomp/Pscav offset adjustments

Check on PMI:
- Cylinder pressure sensor signal

alarms.synopsis: GROUP: Max Pressure Too High - SF Shutdown
alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Max Pressure Too High - SF Shutdown
alarms.long_description: Cylinder pressure exceeds maximum allowed pressure
alarms.cause: - Too early injection of fuel oil or second fuel caused by engine process adjustments, or\n- GI engines: ELGI valve stuck in open position
alarms.effect:
- Dual fuel shutdown
- Engine operation on fuel oil
- Second fuel blocked

WARNING!
Leaking SF injection valve may cause blowback from combustion chamber to SF block, and risk of severe damage to SF components and cylinder cover!
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Cylinder and second fuel pressure curves. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'Cyl. Events' or use SCSU scope to analyse logs located in MAD folder.
- Engine process adjustments, go to 'Engine' -> 'Process Adjustment' -> 'Cylinder Press.' 
- Index calibration mode must be auto for dual fuel operation, go to 'Engine' -> 'Process Adjustment' -> 'Index Calibration' 

WARNING! (GI engines)
If second fuel pressure curve is abnormal (injection starts early when WV is activated or pressure drop is higher than normal), do not attempt to restart dual fuel operation, before engine has been stopped and gas block troubleshooting is completed. Go to 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'Gas Block'.

Reference is made to circular letter or instruction manual showing pressure curves from typical failure situation.

alarms.synopsis: GROUP: Expansion Pressure Too Low - SF Shutdown
alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Expansion Pressure Too Low - SF Shutdown
alarms.long_description: Cylinder expansion pressure is lower than expected
alarms.cause:
- Missing fuel oil injection, or
- Missing second fuel injection, or
- Misfiring, or
- Lower calorific value of sec fuel is too low, or
- Cylinder pressure sensor failure

Missing SF injection can be caused by:
- ELGI/ELFI-L valve failure, or
- Second fuel injection valve failure, or
- ELWI/ELBI valve failure
alarms.effect: - Dual fuel shutdown\n- Engine operation on fuel oil
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Cylinder and second fuel pressure. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'Cyl. Events'
- Alarms on MOP
- Fuel plunger timing and movement. Go to: 'MOP B' -> 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'HCU Events'. 
- Look for ELFI enable signal on 'HCU Events'. 

Check on PMI:
- Cylinder pressure sensor signal. 
- Observe other alarms that might be the cause of the shutdown. Investigate the different possible scenarios

alarms.synopsis: GROUP: Cyl. Pressure Rise Too Fast - SF Shutdown
alarms.data_tree_path: GROUP: Cyl. Pressure Rise Too Fast - SF Shutdown
alarms.long_description: Cylinder pressure rise is too fast
alarms.cause: - Missing pilot oil injection resulting in late and hard ignition of second fuel, or\n- GI engines: ELGI valve stuck in open position
alarms.effect:
- Dual fuel shutdown
- Engine operation on fuel oil
- Second fuel blocked

WARNING!
Leaking SF injection valve may cause blowback from combustion chamber to SF block, and risk of severe damage to SF components and cylinder cover!
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Cylinder and second fuel pressure curves. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'Cyl. Events' or use SCSU scope to analyse logs located in MAD folder.

WARNING! (GI engines)
If second fuel pressure curve is abnormal (injection starts early when WV is activated or pressure drop is higher than normal), do not attempt to restart dual fuel operation, before engine has been stopped and gas block troubleshooting is completed. Go to 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'Gas Block'.

Reference is made to circular letter or instruction manual showing pressure curves from typical failure situation.

If second fuel pressure curves are normal, check fuel plunger stroke measurements on CoCoS and go to 'Engine' -> 'Process Adjustment' -> 'Pilot Oil Profile' and increase offset on cylinder.

LGI engines
Check fuel plunger stroke measurements on CoCoS and go to 'Engine' -> 'Process Adjustment' -> 'Pilot Oil Profile' and increase offset on cylinder.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU*->IO Configuration->Noise Detector->Electrical noise detected
alarms.long_description: Electrical noise has been detected in the ECS system
alarms.cause: - One or more ECS components has intermittent and/or oscillating electric leakage to ship's ground, or\n- ECS system has been subjected to electrical noise from an external source
alarms.effect:
No immediate effect
The fault can generate other consequential alarms in the ECS system, e.g. 
- Exh. Valve Closed Position Changed
- Exh. Valve closing/opening too fast/slow (4 alarms)
- Illegal ELFI/FIVA Position
- ELFI/FIVA Feedback Signal Failure

NOTE: 
Never ignore this alarm. Safety critical issues may arise.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Noise pulse counter by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation
- Cabling, sensors, actuators, Controllers for loose connections or intermittent and/or oscillating electric leakages/short circuits to ground.

To locate an intermittent and/or oscillating electric leakage to ship's ground:
1.Stop engine or reduce rpm to slow down level
If the CCU1 Controller is equipped with IRM Module go to step 7
2. On one controller: Disconnect power supply Connector J1
3. Observe if increase in noise pulse counter has stopped
4. If the increase has stopped, the Controller with intermittent and/or oscillating electric leakage to ship's
ground has been found  skip step 5 and continue to step 6
5. Reconnect the power supply Connector J1 in order for the controller to resume normal function and go back to
step 2, choosing the next controller
6. Reconnect the power supply Connector J1  the controller will resume normal function.
7. Set the CCU1 Controller in TEST MODE by pressing MPC mode button on MOP Maintenance -> System view
I/O. This will stop the controllers normal function.
8. Disconnect connections one at a time (from J2 to J85, - NOT J1), and after each disconnection observe if
increase in noise pulse counter has stopped
9. If increase has stopped, the cable, sensor or actuator with loose connections or intermittent and/or
oscillating electric leakages/short circuits to ground, has been located
10.Revert to basic electrical trouble shooting to repair
11.Set the CCU1 Controller in NORNAL MODE by pressing MPC mode button on MOP Maintenance -> System view I/O

NOTE: 
If a CCU is disconnected or stopped for more than 20 minutes, establishing of emergency lubrication to the affected cylinder is recommended, by fitting of backup lubrication cables from ECU.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU*->Command Handler->HCU Oil Leakage [SLD]
alarms.long_description: Leakage has been detected at the specified HCU
alarms.cause: A leakage is detected in the high pressure fuel pipe.
alarms.effect:
High pressure fuel is present in the outer pipe. 
A leakage in the outer pipe will result in fuel spray onto engine
components and maybe even on personnel. 
The control system provides an option (set by MAN-ES)
for stopping fuel injections on the specific cylinder during this situation.
alarms.suggested_action:
If automatic fuel cut out is not performed by ECS,
manually cut of fuel to that specific cylinder via the chief limiter on MOP.
Reduce engine load to acceptable level with 1 cylinder cut out.
Stop engine when possible and repair high pressure pipe.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU*->Command Handler->HCU Oil Leakage/Relief Disc [SLD]
alarms.long_description: Leakage has been detected at the specified HCU or Relief Disk breakage has been detected at the specified CCU
alarms.cause: A leakage is detected in the high pressure fuel pipe, OR A high pressure in the cylinder have coursed a breakage of the Relief Disk in the relief valve system.
alarms.effect: High pressure fuel is in the outer pipe. A leakage in the outer pipe will result in fuel spray onto engine\ncomponents and maybe even on personnel.  OR Exhaust gas will pass through the Relief Disc hole. \nThe control system provides an option (set by MAN-ES) for stopping fuel injections on the specific cylinder during this situation.
alarms.suggested_action:
If automatic fuel cut out is not performed by ECS,
manually cut of fuel to that specific cylinder via the chief limiter on MOP.
Reduce engine load to acceptable level with 1 cylinder cut out.
Stop engine when possible and repair high pressure pipe.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU*->Command Handler->Relief Disc release [SLD]
alarms.long_description: Relief Disc breakage has been detected at the specified CCU
alarms.cause: A high pressure in the cylinder have coursed a breakage of the Relief Disk in the relief valve system.
alarms.effect: Exhaust gas will pass through the Relief Disk hole. The control system provides an option (set by MAN-ES)\nfor stopping fuel injections on the specific cylinder during this situation.
alarms.suggested_action:
If automatic fuel cut out is not performed by ECS,
manually cut of fuel to that specific cylinder via the chief limiter on MOP.
Reduce engine load to acceptable level with 1 cylinder cut out.
Stop engine when possible and repair high pressure pipe.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU*->Cylinder->Fuel Injection->FO Injection Validation->FO: Burst and Prep sync missed
alarms.long_description: Misfiring coursed by to early Injection Request
alarms.cause: Overload of the CPU, or to early injection request. This could be coursed by wrong parameter setting.
alarms.effect: One fuel injection was missing.
alarms.suggested_action: Check if the parameters has been changed recently.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU*->Cylinder->Fuel Injection->FO Injection Validation->FO: Fuel Plunger Not Returned
alarms.long_description: Fuel plunger did not return to expected position before next injection.
alarms.cause:
- Fuel oil inlet pressure low, or
- Fuel pump suction valve failure, or 
- FIVA valve spool stuck, or 
- Fuel plunger stuck
alarms.effect: Injected fuel amount reduced. \nExhaust gas temperature decreased.\nReduced cylinder performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Fuel supply pressure
- Fuel oil suction valve

Further troubleshooting: 
1. Stop the engine at first opportunity. 
2. Go to 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'HCU'
3. Activate 'Fuel Plunger' and 'Exhaust Valve' to test failing unit 
    
If FIVA movements and exhaust valve are OK: Perform one manual fuel injection attempt.

If manual attempt does not provide any fuel injection: Replace FIVA valve.

- Fuel supply pressure
- Fuel oil suction valve
- Fuel injector valves 

Further troubleshooting:

3. Activate 'Fuel Plunger' and 'Exhaust Valve' to test failing unit 

If FIVA movements and exhaust valve are OK: Perform one manual fuel injection attempt.

If manual attempt does not provide any fuel injection: Replace FIVA valve

alarms.synopsis: FO: Fuel Plunger Stroke Too Low
alarms.data_tree_path: CCU*->Cylinder->Fuel Injection->FO Injection Validation->FO: Fuel Plunger Stroke Too Low
alarms.long_description: Fuel plunger strokes are shorter than ordered by the engine control system.
alarms.cause:
- Injection valve failure, or

- FIVA valve failure, or
- Fuel plunger stuck
alarms.effect: Injected fuel amount incorrect. \nExhaust gas temperature deviation.\nReduced cylinder performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Fuel injection valves
- Fuel viscosity
- Hydraulic oil pressure
Further troubleshooting:
1. Stop the engine at first opportunity.
2. Go to 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'HCU'
3. Activate Fuel Plunger and Exhaust Valve to test failing unit
If FIVA movements and exhaust valve are OK: Perform one manual fuel injection attempt.
If manual attempt does not provide any fuel injection: Replace FIVA valve
If the problem persists: Replace fuel pump plunger and barrel

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU*->Cylinder->Fuel Injection->FO Injection Validation->FO: Illegal Fuel Plng. Move [SLD]
alarms.long_description: The fuel plunger has made an illegal movement. \nRisk of untimed fuel injection.
alarms.cause: - Plunger position sensor or cable failure, or\n- ELFI / FIVA valve failure, or\n- CCU failure
alarms.effect:
No fuel injection due to risk of untimed fuel injection.

For FIVA installations:
- No exhaust valve operation 
- Slowdown is requested
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Fuel plunger position sensor status (Channel 31)
- Fuel plunger position sensor and cabling.

If the sensor is replaced, go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Function Test' to recalibrate the sensor. 

Reactivate fuel injection. Go to 'Engine' -> 'Status' -> 'Cylinder Value Status' -> 'HCU Status and Reset' to reset failing unit. 
Do not reactivate fuel injection until the cylinder unit is considered to be OK.

Further troubleshooting: 
1. Stop the engine at first opportunity. 
2. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'HCU'
3. Test failing unit's fuel plunger operation

If the problem persists, replace or exchange, one part at a time: 
- Fuel plunger position sensor 
- Fuel plunger sensor cabling  
- ELFI / FIVA valve
- CCU

NOTE
Alarm can be overridden by invalidating channel 31 on affected CCU and reactivating fuel injection on 'Maintenance' -> 'System View I/O Test'

alarms.long_description: FO: FIVA/ELFI strokes are less than ordered by the engine control system.
alarms.cause: - FIVA/ELFI valve failure
alarms.effect: Injected fuel amount incorrect. \nExhaust gas temperature deviation.\nReduced cylinder performance.
alarms.suggested_action:

When convenient stop the engine.

If manual attempt does not provide any fuel injection: Replace FIVA/ELFI valve.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU*->Cylinder->Exhaust Valve->Exhaust Valve Supervision->Air Spring Supervision->Air Spring Pressure Low
alarms.long_description: Exhaust valve air spring pressure too low
alarms.cause: - Air spring leakage\n- Air spring supply blocked or shut off\n- Faulty pressure sensor
alarms.effect: Activating the exhaust valve with too low air spring pressure will damage the exhaust valve.
alarms.suggested_action:
Stop Exhaust valve operation immediately on MOP, 'Engine'->'Chief Limiters' -> 'Exhaust Valve Operation' (or power off CCU)

Check:
- Low force Reduction Station spring Air
- Air spring
- Pressure sensor

alarms.synopsis: Exh. Valve Open Stroke Too High
alarms.data_tree_path: CCU*->Cylinder->Exhaust Valve->Exhaust Valve Supervision->Max Stroke Supervision->Exh. Valve Open Stroke Too High
alarms.long_description: Exhaust Valve Open Stroke too high
alarms.cause: - Too low air spring supply pressure, or\n- Air spring leakage, or\n- Faulty exhaustvalve position sensor
alarms.effect: If air spring pressure is too low, continuous operation may result in severe mechanical damage to the exhaust valve air spring disc.
alarms.suggested_action:
If a loud knocking sound is heard from the exhaust valve:
Stop exhaust valve operation immediately on MOP, 'Engine'->'Chief Limiters' -> 'Exhaust Valve Operation' (or power off CCU)


Check: 
- Air spring supply pressure
- Air spring
- Exhaust valve position sensor

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU*->Cylinder->Exhaust Valve->Exhaust Valve Supervision->Exh.V. Close Stroke Low [SLD]
alarms.long_description: The exhaust valve closing stroke is too low (Slowdown)
alarms.cause:
- Accumulator pressure too low, or 
- De-aerating orifice in exhaust valve top blocked, or  
- Non-return valves for exhaust valve actuator oil inlet damaged, or
- No air supply or leaking exhaust valve air spring, or
- Exhaust valve position sensor failure, or
- ELVA/FIVA valve failure

Note:
This alarm also occurs as a consequence of these alarms: 
- Illegal Fuel Plunger Movement 
- Illegal ELFI/FIVA Position
- ELFI/FIVA Feedback Signal Failure
- Frozen IO Detected
alarms.effect: - Fuel injection stopped on affected cylinder.\n- Compression pressure limiter is activated.\n- Slowdown is requested.
alarms.suggested_action:
Please refer to 6645-0320 Running with Cylinders or Turbochargers out of operation.
Check:
- Exhaust valve position sensor.
- Accumulator pressure.
- De-aerating orifice in exhaust valve top.
- Non-return valves for exhaust valve actuator oil inlet.
- Air spring supply pressure and perform drop-down test of exhaust valve spindle.
- ELFI / FIVA valve.

If the parameter "Close Pos Changed Fuel Cut Out" is  active then:

-Increased exhaust gas and valve temperature.

alarms.data_tree_path: CCU*->Cylinder->Cyl Tuning (ACCo)->Cylinder Pmax Supervision->Pmax above allowed value
alarms.long_description: Pmax has exceeded alarm limit.
alarms.cause: Too high Maximum Pressure
alarms.effect: - Increased wear of cylinder liners\n- Risk of breakage of piston rings\n- Too high load on crosshead bearings
alarms.suggested_action:
Immediate Action:
Reduce "Pmax Offset" on actual cylinder unit to lower Pmax below alarm limit.
Troubleshooting:
1.Check that current Pcomp "Deviation" for the actual cylinder unit is within tolerances.
If necessary then carry out adjustments by changing "Pcomp/Pscav Offset" on the actual cylinder unit
manually or via Auto Tuning (Pcomp Deviation ->Pcomp).
2.Check that current Pmax "Deviation" for the actual cylinder unit is within tolerances.
If necessary then carry out adjustments by changing "Pmax Offset" for the actual cylinder unit
manually or via Auto Tuning (Pmax Deviation ->Pmax).
If unable to achieve correct Pcomp (in step 2) then please do not use Auto Tuning functionality and
keep "Pmax Offset" reduced manually on actual cylinder unit below alarm limit.

manually or via Auto Tuning (Pcomp Deviation ->Pcomp).
2.Check that current Pmax "Deviation" for the actual cylinder unit is within tolerances.

manually or via Auto Tuning (Pmax Deviation ->Pmax).

keep "Pmax Offset" reduced manually on actual cylinder unit below alarm limit.

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->IO->Tacho->Tacho set A->Tacho set A failure
alarms.long_description: Abnormal tacho set A signals
alarms.cause:
- Cabling failure (loose connection etc.), or
- Turning wheel sensor failure, or
- Encoder failure, or
- Tacho amplifier A failure, or
- Sensor support console failure, or
- Power failure (ECUA powers tacho set A)

If trigger ring is fitted, this alarm may be caused by:
- Trigger/marker ring is damaged, or
- Trigger/marker sensor failure
alarms.effect: The ECU has switched to tacho set B. \nRedundancy reduced.
alarms.suggested_action:
If only one ECU reports failure: Check Connector J40-J43 on failing ECU
If OK: Replace ECU

If all CCUs and ECUs report tacho failure, check tacho signals on maintenance screen:   
   1. Turn the engine minimum one revolution (by turning gear) 
   2. On failing CCU maintenance screen: Check that channel 40-43 toggle correctly between true and false    
       Channel 40 + 41: twice per revolution 
       Channel 42 + 43: multiple times per revolution (360) 

Perform tacho test on MOP:
Go to Maintenance  -> Function Test -> Tacho 
Follow tacho test instructions

Trace the error by following the signal from :
     Encoder and/or turning wheel marker sensor
        ->Amplifier (TSA-A)
           ->ECU A

If trigger ring is fitted, check:
      a. Trigger/marker ring
      b. Trigger/marker sensor

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->IO->Tacho->Tacho set C->Tacho set C failure

- ECU input channel failure, or
- Failing dual tacho (pulse or marker) sensor, or
- Wrong dual tacho mechanical set-up, or
- Wrong dual tacho parameter set-up in ECS.
alarms.effect: In case of dual tacho: Operation at high speed may lead to RPM hunting if the problem persists.\nIn case of synchrophasing: Synchrophasing operation not possible.\nIn case of RotComp: Vibration reduction disabled.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Inspect dual tacho cabling.
- Inspect dual tacho sensors and mounting brackets.
- Check distance between tacho sensor and tacho ring.
- Check distance between marker sensor and marker ring.
- If the problem persists, contact MAN-ES.

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->IO->Tacho->Delta Tacho B too big
alarms.long_description: The angle difference between tacho system A and B is too big
alarms.cause: The angle between tacho set A and B marker signal exceeds the limit.
alarms.effect: If the system switches from tacho set A to B, maximum pressure deviation may occur.
alarms.suggested_action:
If the alarm 'Tacho set A failure' or 'Tacho set B failure' is active: Ignore this alarm. 

If this alarm is the only tacho alarm:
- At first opportunity: 
     1. Inspect the mechanical condition of the encoders. 
     2. Perform tacho test on MOP:
         Go to 'Maintenance ' -> 'Function Test' -> 'Tacho' 
         Follow tacho test instructions for
         'Fine adjust'.

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->IO->Tacho->Tacho Alignment Err
alarms.long_description: One or both encoders are misaligned
alarms.cause: Tacho set A adjustment differ slightly from tacho set B adjustment.
alarms.effect: Engine performance may be affected
alarms.suggested_action:
If the alarm 'Tacho set A failure' or 'Tacho set B failure' is active: Ignore this alarm. 

If this alarm is the only tacho alarm:
- Check and adjust Pmax. 
- At first opportunity: 
     1. Inspect the mechanical condition of the encoders. 
     2. Readjust the encoders
     3. Perform tacho test on MOP:
         Go to 'Maintenance ' -> 'Function Test' -> 'Tacho' 
         Follow tacho test instructions

NOTE
If encoder A is readjusted or replaced: Perform PMI measurement, and restore tacho offset settings according to 0-diagram

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->IO->Tacho->Marker A Input slip
alarms.long_description: Misalignment between turning wheel sensor and encoders
alarms.cause: a. Turning wheel tacho sensor is damaged or out of adjustment\nb. Both encoders are misaligned compared to turning wheel sensor
alarms.effect: If a: The ECUA Controller has switched to tacho set B\nIf b: Engine performance will be seriously affected. NEVER ignore this alarm!
alarms.suggested_action:
If the alarm 'Tacho set A failure' or 'Tacho set B failure' is active: Ignore this alarm. 

If this alarm is the only tacho alarm, at first opportunity: 
  1. Inspect turning wheel sensor and mounting bracket 
  2. Check distance between sensor and turning wheel
  3. Inspect the mechanical condition of the encoders.

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Propulsion Unit->Engine->Cylinder Lubrication->ACOM Lube->BN Value Feedback Failure
alarms.long_description: BN Value Feedback channel has signal error
alarms.cause: - ACOM Unit Failure: (ACOM System reports internal failure by a 2 mA signal to ECS) \n- Cabling or Signal Failure
alarms.effect: - ACOM System may not be working or is not working correctly\n- ACOM Mix may  not match what is ordered from ECS\n- Ordered BN Value is set to High BN
alarms.suggested_action: - Check Cabling\n- Check ACOM System

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Propulsion Unit->Engine->Cylinder Lubrication->Cylinder lubrication insufficient
alarms.long_description: Requested cylinder lubrication oil injection is greater than one full stroke per revolution on one or more units.
alarms.cause:
The Cylinder Lubrication Oil Feed Rate needed is too high. 

- High operator defined feed rate demand (g/kWh). Cylinder feed rate adjusted to a high value at high engine load, or 
- High sulfur neutralization demand, due to abnormally high sulfur content in Fuel Oil or Fuel Mix, and/or 
- Cylinder lubrication oil used has a too low BN number to support sufficient neutralization.
alarms.effect: The cylinder lubricator will be activated with the highest frequency possible, one per revolution.  \n\nUnder the current conditions the engine cannot maintain requested feed rate, risking excessive wear to the cylinders.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check cylinder lubrication screen and verify that the cylinder lubrication oil settings are in accordance with recommendations. 

Decrease engine load to reduce the amount of cylinder oil needed. 

If the issue is caused by a high sulfur neutralization demand, change cylinder oil to have a higher BN number. 

If problem persist contact MAN Energy Solutions.

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Propulsion Unit->Engine->AutoTuning->Tuning Calculation->ContinuousTuning PI (online FQA)->Online FQA exceeds limits

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Propulsion Unit->Engine->AutoTuning->Tuning Calculation->Sensor Supervision->Cylinder pressure deviation
alarms.long_description: Cylinder pressure measurement deviates more from average value than alarm limit.
alarms.cause:

- Exhaust valve actuator
- FIVA valve

available.
Engine balancing and load distribution might be effected.
alarms.suggested_action: Carry out troubleshooting on above mentioned equipment.

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Propulsion Unit->Engine->AutoTuning->Tuning Calculation->Prise Supervision->Average Prise above allowed value
alarms.long_description: Average Prise has exceeded Pmax-Pcomp alarm limit.
alarms.cause: Too low Compression Pressure or too high Maximum Pressure
alarms.effect: - Increased wear of cylinder liners\n- Risk of breakage of piston rings\n- Too high load on crosshead bearings
alarms.suggested_action:
Immediate Action:
Reduce "Pmax Offset All" to lower average Prise below alarm limit.
Troubleshooting:
1.Check that "Estimated Engine Load" (as shown on MOP) is correct by comparing with PMI
equipment and/or torquemeter.
If incorrect then utilize Fuel Quality feature for adjusting estimated engine load.
2.Check that average "Current Pcomp" and "Ordered Pcomp" are equal (within tolerances).
If necessary then carry out adjustments by changing "Pcomp/Pscav Offset All" manually or via Auto
Tuning (Pcomp mean value).
3.Check that average "Current Pmax" and "Ordered Pmax" are equal (within tolerances).
If necessary then carry out adjustments by changing Pmax Offset All manually or via Auto Tuning
(Pmax mean value).
If unable to achieve correct Pcomp (in step 2) then Pscav might be too low. This could be due to
severe ambient conditions or malfunctioning of exhaust gas bypass etc. Please do not use Auto
Tuning functionality and keep "Pmax Offset All" reduced manually below alarm limit.

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Propulsion Unit->Engine->AutoTuning->Tuning Calculation->Prise Supervision->Cyl 1. Prise above allowed value
alarms.long_description: Prise has exceeded Pmax-Pcomp alarm limit.

alarms.effect: - Increased wear of cylinder liners\n- Risk of breakage of piston rings\n- Too high load on crosshead bearings
alarms.suggested_action:

Troubleshooting:

keep "Pmax Offset" reduced manually on actual cylinder unit below alarm limit.

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Propulsion Unit->Engine->Engine Tuning (ACCo)->FO Index Calibration in Limit
alarms.long_description: Automatic index calibration reached limit
alarms.cause:
- Fuel quality has changed more than allowed by the automatic adjustment.
- Cylinder pressure sensor is failing.
- Failure on fuel equipment, that leads to less injected fuel than ordered.
- If WIF (Water In Fuel) is applied the water content may have changed.
alarms.effect: - The engine load estimation is not fully correct, which may cause fuel index limiters to be incorrect.\n- Prise and Pcomp/Pscav set points might deviate from design values.\n- Cylinder oil feed rate might be incorrect.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- That fuel quality is as expected.
- Check that cylinder pressure sensors (PMI) are working.
- Check Fuel Pumps.
- WIF content is correct.

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Propulsion Unit->Engine->Load Reduction Supervision Group->Pmax Supervision->Average Pmax above allowed value
alarms.long_description: Average Pmax has exceeded alarm limit
alarms.cause: Too high Maximum Pressure
alarms.effect:
- Increased wear of cylinder liners
- Risk of breakage of piston rings
- Too high load on crosshead bearings
- The limiter "Compression pressure" may be activated
alarms.suggested_action:
Immediate Action:
Reduce "Pmax Offset All" to lower average Pmax below alarm limit.
Troubleshooting:
1.Check that "Estimated Engine Load" (as shown on MOP) is correct by comparing with PMI
equipment and/or torquemeter.
If incorrect then utilize Fuel Quality feature for adjusting estimated engine load.
2.Check that average "Current Pcomp" and "Ordered Pcomp" are equal (within tolerances).
If necessary then carry out adjustments by changing "Pcomp/Pscav Offset All" manually or via Auto
Tuning (Pcomp mean value).
3.Check that average "Current Pmax" and "Ordered Pmax" are equal (within tolerances).
If necessary then carry out adjustments by changing "Pmax Offset All" manually or via Auto Tuning
(Pmax mean value).
If unable to achieve correct Pcomp (in step 2) then Pscav might be too high. This could be due to
severe ambient conditions or malfunctioning of exhaust gas bypass etc. Please do not use Auto
Tuning functionality and keep "Pmax Offset All" reduced manually below alarm limit.

alarms.long_description: EEXI Load Limitation is cancelled and is therefore not in effect.
alarms.cause: The cancel command is activated on the bridge or the cancel command signal is failing.
alarms.effect: EEXI Load Limitation is not in effect.\nIn case of signal failure, the limitation is automatically cancelled as a fail safe mode.
alarms.suggested_action:
In case the limitation is manually cancelled:
- The EEXI Load Limitation should only be cancelled for the purpose of securing the safety of the ship or saving life at sea, consistent with regulation 3.1 of MARPOL Annex VI (e.g. operating in adverse weather and ice-infested waters, participation in search and rescue operations, avoidance of pirates and engine maintenance). Deactivate the cancel command as soon as the imminent situation is over.
- It must be logged in the Onboard Management Manual for the EEXI Engine Load Limitation whenever the limitation is cancelled.

In case of signal failure:
- Check the alarm info for the failing signal, or
- EICU controller is not in normal mode.

alarms.cause: This situation arises because the propulsion control system orders too high propeller pitch or engine speed.
alarms.effect: EEXI Load Limitation is exceeded.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Manually reduce the propeller pitch set point or the engine speed set point.
- Check the Near Limit or the Index Margin cable and connectors (from EICU controller) to the propulsion control system.
- Check the propulsion control system reacts on the Near Limit or Index Margin signal sent from the engine control system.
- It must be logged in the Onboard Management Manual for the EEXI Engine Load Limitation whenever the limitation is cancelled.

alarms.synopsis: Slave Pump Started Due to Error(s)
alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Auxiliary Cmd->HPS Command->Self Controlling HPS Cmd->Pump Start/Stop Control->Slave Start/Stop State Machine->Slave Pump Started Due to Error(s)
alarms.long_description: Normally the ECS only starts the Slave pump when the engine load is above a certain limit. In case of certain errors the Slave pump is ordered started
alarms.cause: - Hydraulic Pressure is not valid\n- Setpoint too high compared to actual pressure (Alarm for "Hydr. Press. Regulator High Fail" could also be present!)\n- Missing Pump (Master/Slave pump switched off or missing valid running signals.)
alarms.effect: - No effect if both HPS pumps are running.\n- If only one pump is running the maximum obtainable load will be limited depending on engine configuration. Normally minimum 55% engine load should be possible.\n- If no pumps are running the engine will stop.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Check  Pump start signal:
1) Pump 1 connected to ACU1 Controller Start Up Pump start/stop (ACU1 J61)
2) Pump 2 connected to ACU2 Conttroller Start Up Pump start/stop (ACU2 J61)

- Depending on the type of error that caused this alarm to be raised check the following:
a) Cabling to Hydraulic pressure sensor.
b) Network or tacho alarms on MOP.
c) Hydraulic Pressure Setpoint deviation too large compared to measured pressure.
d) Missing pump running signals.

- Check cabling to Pump 1 and Pump 2 running signals.
(ACU1 Start Up Pump running (ACU1 J45))
(ACU2 Start Up Pump running (ACU2 J45)).

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Auxiliary Cmd->HPS Command->Self Controlling HPS Cmd->Pump Start/Stop Control->Missing Pump (Deviation)
alarms.long_description: ECUA and ECUB are generating differing output values for Missing Pump
alarms.cause: Deviation between redundant input signals to ECU A and ECU B or redundant parameters on ECU A and ECU B
alarms.effect:
Redundancy reduced

No immediate effect on engine operation.
If the reduced redundancy causes Hydraulic Pressure issues other alarms will be raised.
alarms.suggested_action:
Alarm can be reset when engine is stopped

If the problem persists, check:
- ECU cabling 
- ACU cabling
- RCS signals

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Auxiliary Cmd->HPS Command->Self Controlling HPS Cmd->Set Point Adaption->Hydraulic Press. Adaptation [bar]
alarms.long_description: Deviation of Hydraulic Press. Adaptation [bar]
alarms.cause: This can be caused by ECUs having been offline, and is now reconnected.
alarms.effect: This should not have any effect. The value should be overwritten by the controlling ECU and the alarm should no longer be present.
alarms.suggested_action:
No action should be needed.

If the alarm occurs often allowed deviation may be too low - Contact
MAN-ES

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Auxiliary Cmd->HPS Command->Self Controlling HPS Cmd->Set Point Adaption->Hydr. Press. Regulator High Fail
alarms.long_description: The automatic pressure control could not achieve correct pressure. Hydraulic pressure lower than desired.
alarms.cause: HPS pumps do not deliver as high pressure as expected or leakage has increased or electrical connection to HPS is failing.
alarms.effect: Too low pressure may reduce injections and slow down the engine - in extreme cases stop the engine.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check cabling to HPS (e.g. using manual control).
Check pressure sensor.
Check for hydraulic leakages.
Check Swash Plate Indicators.
Check that there are no other alarms for Pumps missing.
Check switch settings on HPS starter cabinets are in normal position.
Check EICU J80 relay:
a) Off then "Slave" pump should be running.
b) ON then "Slave" pump should be stopped.

If all checks above are ok, the HPS proportional valve may need to be recalibrated.

NOTE:
The HPS switch setting on starter cabinet should be set to "Pump 1 Master" or "Pump 2 Master". If the switch is in "Pump 1 & 2" then both HPS pumps should run.

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Auxiliary Cmd->HPS Command->Self Controlling HPS Cmd->Set Point Adaption->Hydr. Press. Regulator Low Fail
alarms.long_description: The automatic pressure control could not achieve correct pressure. Hydraulic pressure higher than desired.
alarms.cause: - HPS pumps deliver higher pressure than expected, or\n- Leakage has decreased.
alarms.effect: Too high pressure can result in excessive electrical power consumption.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check cabling to HPS (e.g. using manual control).
Check pressure sensor.
Check for hydraulic leakages.
Check Swash Plate Indicators.
Check that there are no other alarms for Pumps missing.
Check switch settings on HPS starter cabinets are in normal position.
Check EICU J80 relay:
a) Off then "Slave" pump should be running.
b) ON then "Slave" pump should be stopped.

If all checks above are ok, the HPS proportional valve may need to be recalibrated.

NOTE:
The HPS switch setting on starter cabinet should be set to "Pump 1 Master" or "Pump 2 Master". If the switch is in "Pump 1 & 2" then both HPS pumps should run.

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Auxiliary Cmd->HPS Command->Self Controlling HPS Cmd->Mode Handler (Manual/Auto)->Manual Hydr. Press Control
alarms.long_description: HPS pressure control is manual
alarms.cause: Manual Activated
alarms.effect:
The HPS will "bumpless" change to Manual operation. The pressure setpoint can be overruled by the operator by manually altering the pressure setpoint. The new pressure setpoint will be used until the operator either selects a new setpoint, or returns to Automatic mode.

NOTE:
A large increase in setpoint could trigger the HPS slave pump to start. Therefore it is recommended to limit the steps to about 20 bar.
alarms.suggested_action:
Switch to Automatic operation when manual operation is ended.

NOTE:
In case the ECS setpoint in automatic operation is more than 20 bar above the manual setpoint, increase the manual pressure setpoint, before switching out of manual operation.

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Auxiliary Cmd->HPS Command->Self Controlling HPS Cmd->Pressure Decay Measuring->Hydraulic Pressure fell too quickly
alarms.long_description: Hydraulic pressure fell too quickly after all pumps were stopped.
alarms.cause: Hydraulic leakage or failing accumulator(s).
alarms.effect: Hydraulic leakage or failing accumulators may cause problems when the engine is started again.\nCorrect these failures before attempting normal running.
alarms.suggested_action: Check for Hydraulic leakage and check accumulator pressure.\n- Investigate all HCU's by cutting off relevant valves. Do this one HCU at a time and evaluate leakage result.

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Auxiliary Cmd->HPS Command->Hyd. press. sensor ACU 1 deviates
alarms.long_description: Hydraulic oil pressure sensor (1201-x) on this ACU deviates from the hydraulic oil pressure sensors on the two other ACUs.
alarms.cause:
a. Hydraulic pump failure, or
b. Sensor failure, or
c. ECUA Controller failure, or 
d. Cable failure
alarms.effect:
If a:
Engine performance may be reduced due to reduced hydraulic capacity.

If b, c, and d:
No effect on engine performance.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
a. Hydraulic pump
b. Cabling
c. ECUA Controller
d. Sensor

If a, hydraulic pump failure:
1. Reduce engine load until stable engine performance is achieved
2. Check other alarms
3. Check pump and pump drive shaft

If b, c, or d:
Repair or replace failing part
