alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Auxiliary Cmd->HPS Command->Pump inlet press. low
alarms.long_description: Lubrication oil inlet  pressure is low.
alarms.cause: - Sensor failure, or\n- Lubrication oil supply pump(s) not running, or \n- Inlet valve closed
alarms.effect:
No effect.

NOTE
If system oil pressure drops below shutdown level: 
Engine control system will request shutdown.
alarms.suggested_action: Check:\n- Inlet pressure sensors \n- Lubrication oil supply system(pumps, valves, etc)

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU*->Auxiliary Cmd->HPS Command->Hyd. press. deviates from setpoint
alarms.long_description: The hydraulic pressure deviates from the hydraulic pressure set point calculated by the engine control system
alarms.cause: - Hydraulic system leakage, or\n- Engine driven pump failure, or\n- Engine driven pump calibration failure
alarms.effect: If the hydraulic pressure is lower than the ECS computed setpoint and it continues to decrease, the hydraulic pumps cannot deliver enough oil to maintain the pressure. If the pressure drops below 145 - 150 bar, the ECS is likely to carry out a shutdown. If the pressure is too high, it could lead to increased injection pressure.
alarms.suggested_action:
Reduce engine load until stable engine performance is achieved.

Check:
- Hydraulic system for leaks
- Engine driven pump

If the problem persists: Recalibrate engine driven pump on MOP

alarms.effect: Engine will shut down.\nIt will not be possible to start engine with too low hydraulic oil supply pressure.

alarms.long_description: Sensor signal is out of range
alarms.cause:
- Failure in the cabling to the sensor, or
- Sensor failure, or missing sensor power supply, or
- ECUB Controller input failure, or
- For On/Off type sensors the cause can be a missing or wrong supervision resistor (typically 6.8
kOhm).
alarms.effect: Supervision failure for the insulation detection unit will stop all insulation detection.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Insulation  level by observing the display on the insulation monitor, or
-Insulation level by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation
- Insulation  level trend in CoCoS-EDS if applicable 
- Individual insulation of ECS components (sensors, controllers, actuators, cabling) to determine the cause of leakage
- Refer to ECS trouble shooting guide "test for earth failure in ECS system" for further trouble shooting advise

alarms.data_tree_path: ECU->Propulsion Unit->Engine->Start/Stop Logic->Turning Failed
alarms.long_description: Engine slow turning attempt failed\nEngine was not turned sufficiently
alarms.cause: - Starting air system failure, or\n- ECUB is controlling
alarms.effect: Engine may not be able to start.\nSlow-turning valve is not wired to ECUB and Engine start that require slow-turning will fail.
alarms.suggested_action:
1. Check ECUA is controlling
2. Check slow turning valve
3. Turn engine by turning gear to a different position
4. Retry manual slow turn before new engine start

If the problem persists, check:
- Start air pressure
- Starting air pilot valves
- Starting valves

- CCU is restarting after power off/on, or
- CCU power is off, or
- CCU failure, or
- Both networks are disconnected or failing
alarms.effect:
No fuel injection.
Exhaust valve operation may stop.
Cylinder lubrication may stop. 
Slowdown is requested.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check: 
- CCU power 
- CCU mode (LED is green)
- Network cabling 

If the problem persists: Replace failing CCU

alarms.data_tree_path: EICU*->System->System Status->App. not running on CCU11
alarms.long_description: CCU11 Controller is not in normal operating mode.
alarms.cause: - CCU11 Controller is restarting after power off/on.\n- CCU11 Controller in test or configuration mode.\n- CCU11 Controller failure.
alarms.effect: CCU11 Controller not ready.\nRedundancy reduced.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check CCU11 Controller mode status.

If in test or configuration mode: Restart in normal mode.

If no mode is visible: Wait for CCU11 Controller to finish restart.

If the problem persists: Replace CCU11 Controller.

alarms.data_tree_path: *->System->Global Params. inconsist

alarms.cause: Battery worn out
alarms.effect: If EICUA Controller remains switched on: No effect\n \nIf EICUA Controller is switched off or power is lost: EICUA Controller will loose its time settings
alarms.suggested_action: Replace battery when convenient

alarms.data_tree_path: EICU*->System->Modbus Interface->Modbus Slave failure
alarms.long_description: EICU - RCS communication failure
alarms.cause:
- Cable failure, or
- RCS failure, or
- EICU Modbus failure or
- Commissioning error
alarms.effect: If both EICUs report this alarm: RCS-ECS communication is lost. \nOnly hardwired control and monitoring is available (ECR/LOP)
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Cabling
- RCS

If RCS and cabling is OK: Replace EICU

If both EICUs report this alarm: Restart RCS

alarms.data_tree_path: EICU*->System->Modbus Interface->Modbus Version->Modbus Interface Vers. Number Alarm
alarms.long_description: The Interface Version Number ensures that data on the Modbus line is agreed on by the Modbus Master and Slave systems.
alarms.cause: The Interface Version Number on the Modbus Master and Slave is different
alarms.effect: All data on the Modbus line is invalidated, until the Interface Version Number on Master and Slave side match.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Contact MAN-ES to retrieve the Interface Version Number for the specific plant.
- Check that the Interface Version Number for the specific plant is correct on the Master and Slave side.

RCS to ME-ECS Connections:
- If the Interface Version Number is not correct on the Master side please contact the RCS supplier for setting up the system correctly.

alarms.data_tree_path: EICU*->System->Modbus Interface->Modbus Version->Modbus Configuration Number Alarm
alarms.long_description: The Configuration Number on the Modbus Master and Slave systems must be the same
alarms.cause: The Configuration Number on the Modbus Master and Slave is different
alarms.effect:
RCS to ME-ECS Connections:
- User interface on the RCS is set up based on the engine equipment and Engine Mode.
- Allowed commands and status fields are set up based on the Configuration Number.
Internal ME-ECS Modbus Connections:
- No Effect
alarms.suggested_action:
RCS to ME-ECS Connections:
- Contact MAN-ES to retrieve the Configuration Number for the specific plant.
- Check that the Configuration Number for the specific plant is correct on both the Master and Slave side.
- If the Configuration Number is not correct on the Master side please contact the RCS supplier for setting up the system correctly.

Internal ME-ECS Modbus Connections:
- The Configuration Number should be set to 0 on the Master and Slave side.

alarms.data_tree_path: EICU*->I/O Configuration->ECS Insulation Level Supervision->ECS Insulation level below normal
alarms.long_description: The ECS electric insulation level is below normal service value
alarms.cause: One or more ECS components have increased electric leakage to ship's ground.
alarms.effect: No immediate effect. The alarm can be an indication of beginning deterioration of system components.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Insulation  level by observing the display on the insulation monitor, or
-Insulation level by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation
- Insulation  level trend in CoCoS-EDS if applicable 
- Individual insulation of ECS components (sensors, controllers, actuators, cabling) to determine the cause of leakage
- Refer to ECS trouble shooting guide "test for earth failure in ECS system" for further trouble shooting advise

alarms.data_tree_path: EICU*->I/O Configuration->ECS Insulation Level Supervision->Too low ECS Insulation level
alarms.long_description: The ECS electric insulation level is too low.
alarms.cause: One or more ECS components have too high electric leakage to ship's ground.
alarms.effect:
- The system redundancy is reduced
- The system's resistance against electrical noise is reduced
- Additional insulation faults on opposite polarity can cause blown fuses or short circuits

NOTE: 
Never ignore this alarm. Safety critical issues may arise.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Insulation  level by observing the display on the insulation monitor, or
-Insulation level by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation
- Insulation  level trend in CoCoS-EDS if applicable 
- Individual insulation of ECS components (sensors, controllers, actuators, cabling) to determine the cause of leakage
- Refer to ECS trouble shooting guide "test for earth failure in ECS system" for further trouble shooting advise

NOTE
If more than 3 pumps are installed, pump 4 and 5 are controlled by the ECUs
alarms.effect: - High pressure pumps move to fail safe position (maximum flow in ahead direction)\n- Reversing the engine may not be possible due to insufficient hydraulic pressure
alarms.suggested_action:

NOTE
NEVER ignore this alarm. Safe critical issues may arise!

alarms.data_tree_path: EICU*->ECT Command interface->Commission Mode Req Active (Deviat
alarms.long_description: Deviation between the internal states of EICU A and EICU B regarding whether or not Shop Test Mode should be active.
alarms.cause: Deviation between the MOP commands received by EICU A and EICU B. Maybe due to one of the EICU's being offline when Shop Test Mode was enabled/disabled on the ECT screen.
alarms.effect: Redundancy reduced. In case of one of the EICU's going offline the ECS might make an abrupt change between Shop Test Mode / Not Shop Test Mode.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- EICU cabling

Reselect Shop Test Mode or Not Shop Test Mode on the ECT screen

If the problem persists:
- Restart either EICU A or EICU B when convenient

alarms.data_tree_path: EICU*->ECT Command interface->ECT Mode Act.(Limiters Increased)
alarms.long_description: Shop Test Mode is active
alarms.cause: Shop Test Mode can be toggled on/off from the ECT application. When it is toggled on this alarm is active.
alarms.effect:
The following changes are in effect to allow necessary shop test trials to be carried out:
1: Max Engine Speed has been increased from 105% to 110% MCR
2: Overspeed protection limit change from 106% and 108% MCR to 110% MCR
3: P-scav and Torque limiters have been cancelled
4: Chief index limiter has been raised from 110% to 120%
5: The load program has been disabled
6: Chief Max Speed parameter has been disabled

Changes 1 and 3 are only in effect when ECR is the active control station.
alarms.suggested_action: It is ok for this alarm to be active during shop test when the ECT is being used for engine commissioning.\n\nBefore finishing shop test it is necessary to toggle Shop Test Mode to off via the ECT application.

alarms.cause: - Valve failure, or\n- Feedback failure, or\n- Cabling failure (Opened FB, Closed FB, Open Command)
alarms.effect: ACOM go to Failure Mode. ACOM Bypass Valve (ABV) is commanded to Open. If stucked in: \n- Open position, high BN oil flows to mixing tank. \n- Closed position, no oil flow to mixing tank, which may lead to an engine slow-down
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Valve
- Valve feedback
- Actuator air supply
- Valve cabling (Opened FB, Closed FB, Open Command)

Further troubleshooting.
1. ABV is commanded to open. If stucked in closed position, try to open it manually.
2. Operate valve by changing OMCU Controller mode to test. Avoid doing this while the engine is running.
3. Observe feedback during valve operation.

alarms.effect: ACOM go to Failure Mode. ACOM Bypass Valve (ABV) Opens
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Valve
- Valve feedback
- Valve cabling (Opened FB, Closed FB, Open Command)

Further troubleshooting.
1. Operate valve by changing OMCU Controller mode to test. Avoid doing this while the engine is running.
2. Observe feedback during valve operation

alarms.effect: ACOM go to Failure Mode. ACOM Bypass Valve (ABV) Opens
alarms.suggested_action:
Check: 
- Cabling 
- Inlet Filter 
- Inlet Valve 
- If problem persists, replace level switch

alarms.data_tree_path: OMCU->ACOM Control->Low BN Tank->Pump (VFD) Control->Remote Local Fail Alarm

alarms.suggested_action: - Check if VFD is set to 'Local' - switch back to 'Remote'. \n- If VFD is not set to 'Local' check local info on VFD monitor.\n- If no local alarm on VFD check cabling

alarms.data_tree_path: OMCU->ACOM Control->Low BN Tank->Temperature Control->Temperature Sensor->Temperature Sensor Above Max

alarms.suggested_action: Check: \n If ACOM is in Failure Mode or it has recently recovered from it alarm is expected and safe to ignore, else \n Check Level Transmitter

alarms.data_tree_path: OMCU->ACOM Control->Pump (VFD) Speed Calculation->Term: Mix BN Order (from ECU)->Signal Value or Status Overwritten

alarms.suggested_action: - Check serial connections from circuit breakers to OMCU Controller,\n- Check fan and mixing motor

alarms.data_tree_path: SACU1->System->Modbus Interface->Modbus Slave failure

alarms.cause:
- Cable failure, or

alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Cabling
- RCS

If both EICUs report this alarm: Restart RCS

Replace SACU1 Controller or contact MAN-ES

alarms.effect: - All data on the Modbus line is invalidated. Control and Status values between the Master and Slave will not be available.
alarms.suggested_action: Check:\n- Cabling\n- Check that SACU1 Controller are running in Normal Mode

alarms.cause: - Power failure, or\n- Signal failure
alarms.effect: - No direct effect on dual fuel operation
alarms.suggested_action: Check for other alarms. If valves in second fuel valve train are failing power has actually failed.

alarms.data_tree_path: SACU1->IO Configuration->ECS Insulation Level Superv->ECS Insulation level below normal
alarms.long_description: The ECS electric insulation level is below normal service value
alarms.cause: One or more ECS components have increased electric leakage to ship's ground.
alarms.effect: No immediate effect. The alarm can be an indication of beginning deterioration of system components.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Insulation  level by observing the display on the insulation monitor, or
-Insulation level by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation
- Insulation  level trend in CoCoS-EDS if applicable 
- Individual insulation of ECS components (sensors, controllers, actuators, cabling) to determine the cause of leakage
- Refer to ECS trouble shooting guide "test for earth failure in ECS system" for further trouble shooting advise

alarms.data_tree_path: SACU1->IO Configuration->ECS Insulation Level Superv->Too low ECS Insulation level
alarms.long_description: The ECS electric insulation level is too low.
alarms.cause: One or more ECS components have too high electric leakage to ship's ground.
alarms.effect:
- The system redundancy is reduced
- The system's resistance against electrical noise is reduced
- Additional insulation faults on opposite polarity can cause blown fuses or short circuits

NOTE: 
Never ignore this alarm. Safety critical issues may arise.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Insulation  level by observing the display on the insulation monitor, or
-Insulation level by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation
- Insulation  level trend in CoCoS-EDS if applicable 
- Individual insulation of ECS components (sensors, controllers, actuators, cabling) to determine the cause of leakage
- Refer to ECS trouble shooting guide "test for earth failure in ECS system" for further trouble shooting advise

alarms.synopsis: Hyd Press Too Low For Seal Oil
alarms.data_tree_path: SACU1->SEAL: Seal Oil->Hyd Press Too Low For Seal Oil
alarms.long_description: Hydraulic oil pressure below seal oil pressure setpoint
alarms.cause: HPS pumps do not deliver as high pressure as expected or leakage has increased or electrical connection to HPS is failing.
alarms.effect: Seal Oil Valve is closed to prevent seal oil draining backwards
alarms.suggested_action:
Check cabling to HPS (e.g. using manual control).
Check pressure sensor.
Check for hydraulic leakages.
Check Swash Plate Indicators.
Check that there are no other alarms for Pumps missing.
Check switch settings on HPS starter cabinets are in normal position.
Check EICU J80 relay:
a) Off then "Slave" pump should be running.
b) ON then "Slave" pump should be stopped.

If all checks above are ok, the HPS proportional valve may need to be recalibrated.

NOTE:
The HPS switch setting on starter cabinet should be set to "Pump 1 Master" or "Pump 2 Master". If the switch is in "Pump 1 & 2" then both HPS pumps should run.

alarms.data_tree_path: SACU1->ECU Com->No Telegram from ECUA
alarms.long_description: SACU1 did not receive a telegram network message from ECUA.\n\nTelegram is sent periodically and contains information about engine loads, dual fuel operation etc.
alarms.cause:
If SACU1 reports this alarm continuously:
- ECUA failure

If SACU1 reports this alarm randomly:
- Network failure
alarms.effect: Values from ECUB are used. If ECUA also fails dual fuel operation will be stopped.
alarms.suggested_action:
If SACU1 continues to report this alarm, check: 
- ECUA
- Network cabling

If SACU1 randomly reports this failure, check:
- Network status. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Network Status'
- Network cabling and terminating resistors.
- For earth fault

alarms.data_tree_path: SACU2->IO Configuration->ECS Insulation Level Supervision->ECS Insulation level below normal
alarms.long_description: The ECS electric insulation level is below normal service value
alarms.cause: One or more ECS components have increased electric leakage to ship's ground.
alarms.effect: No immediate effect. The alarm can be an indication of beginning deterioration of system components.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Insulation  level by observing the display on the insulation monitor, or
-Insulation level by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation
- Insulation  level trend in CoCoS-EDS if applicable 
- Individual insulation of ECS components (sensors, controllers, actuators, cabling) to determine the cause of leakage
- Refer to ECS trouble shooting guide "test for earth failure in ECS system" for further trouble shooting advise

alarms.data_tree_path: SACU2->IO Configuration->ECS Insulation Level Supervision->Too low ECS Insulation level

alarms.cause: One or more ECS components have too high electric leakage to ship's ground.
alarms.effect:
- The system redundancy is reduced
- The system's resistance against electrical noise is reduced
- Additional insulation faults on opposite polarity can cause blown fuses or short circuits

NOTE: 
Never ignore this alarm. Safety critical issues may arise.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Insulation  level by observing the display on the insulation monitor, or
-Insulation level by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation
- Insulation  level trend in CoCoS-EDS if applicable

alarms.cause: - Seal oil pump failure, or\n - Seal oil leakage\n - Low pressure seal oil valve failure
alarms.effect: - Dual fuel stop\n- Engine operation on fuel oil
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
 - For seal oil leakages
 - Failing seal oil pump
 - Failing low pressure seal oil valve

alarms.data_tree_path: SACU2->SOU: Seal Oil Unit->Tank Vent Ctrl Failure
alarms.long_description: Electric motor cannot be controlled by the engine control system
alarms.cause:
- Electric motor switchboard is off or manually set to 'Local', or
- Electric motor switch board failure, or
- Switchboard feedback failure, or
- Cabling failure
alarms.effect: If the failure is in the feedback part only: No effect\nElse: No ECS control of electric motor
alarms.suggested_action:
1. Check that the operation control switch at the switchboard is set to ''Remote'
2. Check switchboard, main breaker and overcurrent protection relay
3. Check cabling

If all is OK: Set switch to 'Off' and wait a few seconds. 
Reset switch to ''Remote'

- Engine operation on fuel oil

- Sensor
- Inert Gas System Pressure

alarms.data_tree_path: SACU2->RPPB: Return Pipe Purge Block->Purge Block Train Press Drift
alarms.long_description: Purge Block Train Press at PT6346 drifts during Purge Block Test
alarms.cause:
Mechanical or cabling failure on:

- Return Block Supply Valve, or
- Return Block Bleed Valve, or
- Return Block Inlet Valve

- Sensor PT6346 failure
alarms.effect:
Purging with Return Purge Block Fails

During dual fuel operation:
- Dual fuel stop
- Engine operation on fuel oil

During fuel oil operation:
- Dual fuel operation unavailable
alarms.suggested_action:
Check for additional alarms on Return Purge Block. The combination of alarms may tell which valve is not functioning.

Check valves for:
- Cabling
- Mechanical function
- Leakage between Valve house and spindle

Test Mode:
On SACU-2 Set valve I/O channels in Test Mode and check function

- Check Sensor PT6346

alarms.data_tree_path: SACU2->SPCU Com->No Telegram From SPCU
alarms.long_description:
SACU-2 did not receive a telegram network message from SPCU.

Telegram is sent periodically and contains:
- Cool Seal Oil Run Command
- Open cool oil valve and seal oil valve Commands
- LGI Detected in Return Pipe Feedback
- Return Purge Block Commands
alarms.cause:
If SACU-2 reports this alarm continuously:
- SPCU failure

If SACU-2 reports this alarm randomly:
- Network failure
alarms.effect:
During dual fuel Operation:
- Dual fuel stop
- Engine operation on fuel oil

During fuel oil operation:
- Dual fuel operation unavailable
alarms.suggested_action:
If SACU-2 continues to report this alarm, check:
- SPCU
- Network cabling

If SACU-2 randomly reports this failure, check:
- Network status. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Network Status'
- Network cabling and terminating resistors.
- For ground failure

alarms.data_tree_path: SACU2->SPSU Com->No Telegram From SPSU
alarms.long_description:
SACU-2 did not receive a telegram network message from SPSU.

Telegram is sent periodically and contains: 
- HC in Cool/Seal Oil Tank Detection
- Cooling Oil Pressure
- Cooling Oil Tank Temperature
- Cool/Seal Oil Tank Min./Max. Shutdown Level
alarms.cause:
If SACU-2 reports this alarm continuously:
- SPSU failure

If SPSU reports this alarm randomly:
- Network failure
alarms.effect:

- Dual fuel stop
- Engine operation on fuel oil

During fuel oil operation:
- Dual fuel operation unavailable
alarms.suggested_action:
If SACU-2 continues to report this alarm, check:

- Network cabling

If SPSU randomly reports this failure, check:
- Network status. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Network Status'
- Network cabling and terminating resistors.
- For ground failure

alarms.data_tree_path: SCSU*->IO Configuration->ECS Insulation Level Supervision->ECS Insulation level below normal
alarms.long_description: The ECS electric insulation level is below normal service value
alarms.cause: One or more ECS components have increased electric leakage to ship's ground.
alarms.effect: No immediate effect. The alarm can be an indication of beginning deterioration of system components.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Insulation  level by observing the display on the insulation monitor, or
-Insulation level by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation
- Insulation  level trend in CoCoS-EDS if applicable 
- Individual insulation of ECS components (sensors, controllers, actuators, cabling) to determine the cause of leakage
- Refer to ECS trouble shooting guide "test for earth failure in ECS system" for further trouble shooting advise

alarms.data_tree_path: SCSU*->IO Configuration->ECS Insulation Level Supervision->Too low ECS Insulation level
alarms.long_description: The ECS electric insulation level is too low.
alarms.cause: One or more ECS components have increased electric leakage to ship's ground.
alarms.effect:
- The system redundancy is reduced
- The system's resistance against electrical noise is reduced
- Additional insulation faults on opposite polarity can cause blown fuses or short circuits

NOTE: 
Never ignore this alarm. Safety critical issues may arise.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Insulation  level by observing the display on the insulation monitor, or
-Insulation level by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation
- Insulation  level trend in CoCoS-EDS if applicable 
- Individual insulation of ECS components (sensors, controllers, actuators, cabling) to determine the cause of leakage
- Refer to ECS trouble shooting guide "test for earth failure in ECS system" for further trouble shooting advise

alarms.data_tree_path: SCSU*->Cylinder Safety->Cyl 2: Status->Cyl 2: Alarms->Cyl 2: ELBI FB Delay Failure
alarms.long_description: ELBI Closed Feedback Sensor deviates from ELBI Valve Open Command Signal
alarms.cause:
- ELBI Closed Feedback Sensor Failure (J334-337)

- ELBI Valve Failure (closes to slowly or does not close) (J370-373)

- Cabling Failure on Command Signals (J370-373) or Feedback signals (J334-337)
alarms.effect: - Dual fuel shutdown\n- Engine operation on fuel oil
alarms.suggested_action:
Check: 
- Cabling (Valve or Feedback)
- ELBI Valve
- ELBI Feedback Sensor

If problem persists:
1. Operate valve by changing SCSU mode to test.
2. Observe feedback during valve operation

If command and feedback match, the ELBI feedback sensor is possibly too slow and must be replaced.

If command and feedback do not match, either the ELBI Feedback sensor is failing or the ELBI Valve is failing and one or both must be replaced.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCSU*->Cylinder Safety->Cyl 3: Status->Cyl 3: Second fuel blocked
alarms.long_description: Second fuel operation on current cylinder is blocked
alarms.cause:
SCSU cylinder supervision has detected a situation, which may potentially damage the engine if not treated correctly.
- Cylinder pressure supervision has detected too high max pressure or too fast pressure rise, or
- GI engines: SF channel pressure supervision has detected SF pressure drop test failure, SF pressure curve fit failure or SF pressure range failure.
- LGI engines: SF channel pressure sensor has detected a leaking FBIV sliding- and suction-valves
alarms.effect:
- Dual fuel operation unavailable, 
- Manual assembly test and manual purge of second fuel system is unavailable.


WARNING!
Leaking SF injection valve may cause blowback from combustion chamber to SF block, and risk of severe damage to SF components and cylinder cover!
alarms.suggested_action:
RECOMMENDATION if leaking SF injection valve:
- Cut-out fuel oil injection on this cylinder, or 
- Stop and exchange the damaged valve.

DO NOT start dual fuel operation until this failure is located and repaired.

DO NOT reset second fuel block before failure is located.

Check:
- Other alarms stating cause of SF shutdown and recommended action
- Cylinder and second fuel pressure curves. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'Cyl. Events' or use SCSU scope to analyse logs located in MAD folder.

If failure is identified as a missing pilot, adjust pilot injection and reset second fuel blocked.

If another failure is located in second fuel system, perform troubleshooting on second fuel block with stopped engine before reset of second fuel block.

To reset second fuel block, go to: 'Engine'->'Status' -> 'Cylinder Value Status' and reset 'Second Fuel Block'.

- Misfiring, or
- Lower calorific value of sec fuel is too low, or
- Cylinder pressure sensor failure

- ELGI/ELFI-L valve failure, or
- Second fuel injection valve failure, or
- ELWI/ELBI valve failure

alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Cylinder and second fuel pressure. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'Cyl. Events'
- Alarms on MOP
- Fuel plunger timing and movement. Go to: 'MOP B' -> 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'HCU Events'. 
- Look for ELFI enable signal on 'HCU Events'. 

Check on PMI:
- Cylinder pressure sensor signal. 
- Observe other alarms that might be the cause of the shutdown. Investigate the different possible scenarios

alarms.data_tree_path: SCSU*->Cylinder Safety->Cyl 5: Status->Cyl 5: Second fuel blocked
alarms.long_description: Second fuel operation on current cylinder is blocked
alarms.cause:
SCSU cylinder supervision has detected a situation, which may potentially damage the engine if not treated correctly.
- Cylinder pressure supervision has detected too high max pressure or too fast pressure rise, or
- GI engines: SF channel pressure supervision has detected SF pressure drop test failure, SF pressure curve fit failure or SF pressure range failure.
- LGI engines: SF channel pressure sensor has detected a leaking FBIV sliding- and suction-valves
alarms.effect:
- Dual fuel operation unavailable, 
- Manual assembly test and manual purge of second fuel system is unavailable.


WARNING!
Leaking SF injection valve may cause blowback from combustion chamber to SF block, and risk of severe damage to SF components and cylinder cover!
alarms.suggested_action:
RECOMMENDATION if leaking SF injection valve:
- Cut-out fuel oil injection on this cylinder, or 
- Stop and exchange the damaged valve.

DO NOT start dual fuel operation until this failure is located and repaired.

DO NOT reset second fuel block before failure is located.

Check:
- Other alarms stating cause of SF shutdown and recommended action
- Cylinder and second fuel pressure curves. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'Cyl. Events' or use SCSU scope to analyse logs located in MAD folder.

If failure is identified as a missing pilot, adjust pilot injection and reset second fuel blocked.

If another failure is located in second fuel system, perform troubleshooting on second fuel block with stopped engine before reset of second fuel block.

To reset second fuel block, go to: 'Engine'->'Status' -> 'Cylinder Value Status' and reset 'Second Fuel Block'.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCSU*->Cylinder Safety->Cyl 5: Status->Cyl 5: Alarms->Cyl 5: Compression Press Too Low
alarms.long_description: Compression pressure is too low for SF injection.
alarms.cause:
- Leaking exhaust valve, or 
- Piston ring blow-by, or
- Air spring failure, or 
- Exhaust valve actuator failure, or 
- Exhaust valve damper failure, or  
- ELFI / FIVA valve failure, or
- Pcomp/Pscav offset, or
- Cylinder pressure sensor failure
alarms.effect: - Dual fuel shutdown\n- Engine operation on fuel oil
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Cylinder pressure. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'Cyl. Events'
- Alarms on MOP
- Exhaust valve closing. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'HCU Events'
- Air spring
- Exhaust valve actuator
- Exhaust valve oil cylinder
- ELFI / FIVA valve
- Pcomp/Pscav offset adjustments

Check on PMI:
- Cylinder pressure sensor signal

alarms.data_tree_path: SCSU*->Cylinder Safety->Cyl 5: Status->Cyl 5: Alarms->Cyl 5: Max Pressure Too High
alarms.long_description: Cylinder pressure exceeds maximum allowed pressure
alarms.cause: - Too early injection of fuel oil or second fuel caused by engine process adjustments, or\n- GI engines: ELGI valve stuck in open position
alarms.effect:
- Dual fuel shutdown
- Engine operation on fuel oil
- Second fuel blocked

WARNING!
Leaking SF injection valve may cause blowback from combustion chamber to SF block, and risk of severe damage to SF components and cylinder cover!
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Cylinder and second fuel pressure curves. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'Cyl. Events' or use SCSU scope to analyse logs located in MAD folder.
- Engine process adjustments, go to 'Engine' -> 'Process Adjustment' -> 'Cylinder Press.' 
- Index calibration mode must be auto for dual fuel operation, go to 'Engine' -> 'Process Adjustment' -> 'Index Calibration' 

WARNING! (GI engines)
If second fuel pressure curve is abnormal (injection starts early when WV is activated or pressure drop is higher than normal), do not attempt to restart dual fuel operation, before engine has been stopped and gas block troubleshooting is completed. Go to 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'Gas Block'.

Reference is made to circular letter or instruction manual showing pressure curves from typical failure situation.

- Cylinder pressure sensor failure

- ELGI/ELFI-L valve failure, or
- Second fuel injection valve failure, or
- ELWI/ELBI valve failure

- Alarms on MOP
- Fuel plunger timing and movement. Go to: 'MOP B' -> 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'HCU Events'.

Check on PMI:
- Cylinder pressure sensor signal.

- ELBI Valve Failure (closes to slowly or does not close) (J370-373)

- Cabling Failure on Command Signals (J370-373) or Feedback signals (J334-337)
alarms.effect: - Dual fuel shutdown\n- Engine operation on fuel oil
alarms.suggested_action:
Check: 
- Cabling (Valve or Feedback)
- ELBI Valve
- ELBI Feedback Sensor

If problem persists:
1. Operate valve by changing SCSU mode to test.
2. Observe feedback during valve operation

If command and feedback match, the ELBI feedback sensor is possibly too slow and must be replaced.

If command and feedback do not match, either the ELBI Feedback sensor is failing or the ELBI Valve is failing and one or both must be replaced.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCSU*->Cylinder Safety->Cyl 6: Status->Cyl 6: Second fuel blocked
alarms.long_description: Second fuel operation on current cylinder is blocked
alarms.cause:
SCSU cylinder supervision has detected a situation, which may potentially damage the engine if not treated correctly.
- Cylinder pressure supervision has detected too high max pressure or too fast pressure rise, or
- GI engines: SF channel pressure supervision has detected SF pressure drop test failure, SF pressure curve fit failure or SF pressure range failure.
- LGI engines: SF channel pressure sensor has detected a leaking FBIV sliding- and suction-valves
alarms.effect:
- Dual fuel operation unavailable, 
- Manual assembly test and manual purge of second fuel system is unavailable.


WARNING!
Leaking SF injection valve may cause blowback from combustion chamber to SF block, and risk of severe damage to SF components and cylinder cover!
alarms.suggested_action:
RECOMMENDATION if leaking SF injection valve:
- Cut-out fuel oil injection on this cylinder, or 
- Stop and exchange the damaged valve.

DO NOT start dual fuel operation until this failure is located and repaired.

DO NOT reset second fuel block before failure is located.

Check:
- Other alarms stating cause of SF shutdown and recommended action
- Cylinder and second fuel pressure curves. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'Cyl. Events' or use SCSU scope to analyse logs located in MAD folder.

If failure is identified as a missing pilot, adjust pilot injection and reset second fuel blocked.

If another failure is located in second fuel system, perform troubleshooting on second fuel block with stopped engine before reset of second fuel block.

To reset second fuel block, go to: 'Engine'->'Status' -> 'Cylinder Value Status' and reset 'Second Fuel Block'.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCSU*->Cylinder Safety->Cyl 9: Status->Cyl 9: Second fuel blocked
alarms.long_description: Second fuel operation on current cylinder is blocked
alarms.cause:
SCSU cylinder supervision has detected a situation, which may potentially damage the engine if not treated correctly.
- Cylinder pressure supervision has detected too high max pressure or too fast pressure rise, or
- GI engines: SF channel pressure supervision has detected SF pressure drop test failure, SF pressure curve fit failure or SF pressure range failure.
- LGI engines: SF channel pressure sensor has detected a leaking FBIV sliding- and suction-valves
alarms.effect:
- Dual fuel operation unavailable, 
- Manual assembly test and manual purge of second fuel system is unavailable.


WARNING!
Leaking SF injection valve may cause blowback from combustion chamber to SF block, and risk of severe damage to SF components and cylinder cover!
alarms.suggested_action:
RECOMMENDATION if leaking SF injection valve:
- Cut-out fuel oil injection on this cylinder, or 
- Stop and exchange the damaged valve.

DO NOT start dual fuel operation until this failure is located and repaired.

DO NOT reset second fuel block before failure is located.

Check:
- Other alarms stating cause of SF shutdown and recommended action
- Cylinder and second fuel pressure curves. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'Cyl. Events' or use SCSU scope to analyse logs located in MAD folder.

If failure is identified as a missing pilot, adjust pilot injection and reset second fuel blocked.

If another failure is located in second fuel system, perform troubleshooting on second fuel block with stopped engine before reset of second fuel block.

To reset second fuel block, go to: 'Engine'->'Status' -> 'Cylinder Value Status' and reset 'Second Fuel Block'.

Check:
- Actuator cabling
- If bypass valve can move
- Actuator end stop switches

alarms.suggested_action: Switch back to automatic control when manual operation is complete, 'Auxiliaries' -> 'Scavenge Air' (Chief level access required)

alarms.data_tree_path: SCU->Exhaust Gas Bypass/Valves->Var. EGB Setpoint Deviation->Position deviation (Reset Required)

- MPC failure

Last valid valve position set point is used. 

NOTE 
If valve is stuck in closed or partly closed position, keep the engine load below 75%
alarms.suggested_action:

alarms.synopsis: PT Flow Area Above Max Allowed
alarms.data_tree_path: SCU*->Waste Heat Recovery 2->PT Flow Area Above Max Allowed
alarms.long_description: Power Turbine control valve exceeds the Allowed Level for too long time.
alarms.cause:
Power Turbine has not reduced opening of the control valve to allowed level.
Signals -allowed and actual Power Turbine have wrong values.

The signal "PT Valve Actual Position" signal  has a value above the signal  "Available Exh. Energy
alarms.effect: Low scavenging air pressure - leading to low efficiency.\nHigh exhaust and combustion chamber temperatures leading to increased wear on components.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check: 
- WHR/PMS system.
- signal levels on WHR and ECS systems.
Reduce Power Turbine control valve opening if possible.
If Power turbine control valve continues to operate significantly above allowed level, Power Turbine should be disabled in the load ranges where it operates above limit

alarms.synopsis: TC PTO Power Above Max Allowed
alarms.data_tree_path: SCU*->Waste Heat Recovery 2->TC PTO Power Above Max Allowed
alarms.long_description: TC PTO power has exceeded the Allowed Level for too long time.
alarms.cause: TC PTO system has not reduced power take out to allowed level.\nSignals -Max Allowed and Actual TC PTO power have incorrect values.\nThe signal " TC PTO Actual Power" has a value above the signal "TC PTO, Max Allowed Power
alarms.effect: Low scavenging air pressure - leading to low efficiency.\nHigh exhaust and combustion chamber temperatures leading to increased thermal stress on engine\ncomponents.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- TC PTO system/PMS system.
- Signal levels on TC PTO and ECS systems.
Reduce TC PTO power if possible.
If TC PTO system continues to operate significantly above allowed level, TC PTO system should be
disabled in the load ranges where it operates above limit

NOTE
If engine load above 75% is required, open variable turbocharger/bypass valve mechanically or via MOP

alarms.effect: Insufficient lube oil being delivered to TC which may result in damage to TC.
alarms.suggested_action: - Check TC Lube Oil Inlet Pressure Reduction Valve, and its cabling.\n- Check TC Lube Oil Inlet Pressure Transducer, and its cabling.\n- Check for leaks.

- Check TC Lube Oil Inlet Pressure Reduction Valve, and its cabling.
- Check TC Lube Oil Inlet Pressure Transducer, and its cabling.
- Check for leaks.

alarms.suggested_action: - Check TC Lube Oil Inlet Pressure Reduction Valve, and its cabling.\n- Check TC Lube Oil Inlet Pressure Reduction Flow Control Valve.\n- Check TC Lube Oil Inlet Pressure Transducer, and its cabling.

alarms.data_tree_path: SPCU->SFCB: Cylinder Block->Second Fuel Blocked
alarms.long_description: Second Fuel Injection on one or more cylinders are blocked
alarms.cause:
SCSU cylinder supervision has detected a situation, which may potentially damage the engine if not treated correctly.
- Cylinder pressure supervision has detected too high max pressure or too fast pressure rise, or
- GI engines: SF channel pressure supervision has detected SF pressure drop test failure, SF pressure curve fit failure or SF pressure range failure.
- LGI engines: SF channel pressure sensor has detected a leaking FBIV sliding- and suction-valves
alarms.effect:
- Dual fuel operation unavailable, 
- Manual assembly test and manual purge of second fuel system is unavailable.


WARNING!
Leaking SF injection valve may cause blowback from combustion chamber to SF block, and risk of severe damage to SF components and cylinder cover!
alarms.suggested_action:
RECOMMENDATION if leaking SF injection valve:
- Cut-out fuel oil injection on this cylinder, or 
- Stop and exchange the damaged valve.

DO NOT start dual fuel operation until this failure is located and repaired.

DO NOT reset second fuel block before failure is located.

Check:
- Other alarms stating cause of SF shutdown and recommended action
- Cylinder and second fuel pressure curves. Go to: 'Maintenance' -> 'Troubleshooting' -> 'Cyl. Events' or use SCSU scope to analyse logs located in MAD folder.

If failure is identified as a missing pilot, adjust pilot injection and reset second fuel blocked.

If another failure is located in second fuel system, perform troubleshooting on second fuel block with stopped engine before reset of second fuel block.

To reset second fuel block, go to: 'Engine'->'Status' -> 'Cylinder Value Status' and reset 'Second Fuel Block'.

alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Insulation  level by observing the display on the insulation monitor, or
-Insulation level by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation
- Insulation  level trend in CoCoS-EDS if applicable

- Refer to ECS trouble shooting guide "test for earth failure in ECS system" for further trouble shooting advise

- Additional insulation faults on opposite polarity can cause blown fuses or short circuits

NOTE:
